{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_5a8d18cd8d804af48e252dee","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# bead-forge Implementation Plan\n2\t\n3\t> **User-facing documentation:** [`../README.md`](../README.md) — overview, command reference, NEEDLE integration guide, and hero image.\n4\t\n5\t## Overview\n6\t\n7\t**bead-forge** (`bf`) is a Rust binary that replaces `br` (beads_rust). SQLite is the live database — all reads and writes go through it. `issues.jsonl` is a git-synced artifact exported on demand: one entry per bead, committed to the repo for backup, sharing, and recovery. Concurrent claiming is handled by SQLite's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction — no server, no daemon, no flock required.\n8\t\n9\t## Core Principles\n10\t\n11\t1. **SQLite is the live store** — all mutations are SQL writes; reads are SQL queries. Fast, concurrent-read, serialized-write via WAL mode.\n12\t2. **JSONL is the git artifact** — exported on `bf sync`, committed to git, one entry per bead. Used for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. ~~Never written during normal operation.~~ *(Amended 2026-07-21, Phase 7.1: with `sync.auto_flush` — default on — every successful mutation incrementally exports the changed beads to JSONL, so the artifact tracks the live store instead of trailing it. `bf sync --flush-only` remains the explicit checkpoint and the recovery path when auto-flush fails. Read-only commands still never write.)*\n13\t3. **Drop-in CLI** — all `br` commands work under `bf` with the same flags and output formats\n14\t4. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim** — the read-score-update sequence runs inside a single SQLite write transaction, eliminating the race condition `br` has without requiring flock or a daemon\n15\t\n16\t---\n17\t\n18\t## Phase 1: Core Library — Data Model & JSONL Import/Export\n19\t\n20\t### 1.1 Data Model (`src/model.rs`)\n21\t\n22\tPort the exact `Issue`, `Status`, `Priority`, `IssueType`, `Dependency`, `DependencyType`, `Comment`, and `Event` structs from beads_rust with identical Serde attributes. This is the wire format — every field, every `skip_serializing_if`, every rename must match.\n23\t\n24\tKey structs and their JSONL serialization:\n25\t\n26\t```\n27\tStatus:       open | in_progress | blocked | deferred | draft | closed | tombstone | pinned | Custom(String)\n28\tPriority:     transparent i32 (0=Critical, 4=Backlog)\n29\tIssueType:    task | bug | feature | epic | chore | docs | question | Custom(String)\n30\tDependency:   { issue_id, depends_on_id, type (renamed from dep_type), created_at, created_by?, metadata?, thread_id? }\n31\tComment:      { id: i64, issue_id, author, text (renamed from body), created_at }\n32\tEvent:        { id: i64, issue_id, event_type, actor, old_value?, new_value?, comment?, created_at }\n33\t```\n34\t\n35\tIssue fields (alphabetical by JSON key):\n36\t```\n37\tid, title, description?, design?, acceptance_criteria?, notes?,\n38\tstatus, priority, issue_type, assignee?, owner?, estimated_minutes?,\n39\tcreated_at, created_by?, updated_at, closed_at?, close_reason?,\n40\tclosed_by_session?, due_at?, defer_until?, external_ref?,\n41\tsource_system?, source_repo, deleted_at?, deleted_by?, delete_reason?,\n42\toriginal_type?, compaction_level (default 0), compacted_at?,\n43\tcompacted_at_commit?, original_size?, sender?, ephemeral (default false),\n44\tpinned (default false), is_template (default false),\n45\tlabels: Vec<String>, dependencies: Vec<Dependency>, comments: Vec<Comment>\n46\t```\n47\t\n48\t### 1.2 JSONL Import (`src/jsonl.rs`)\n49\t\n50\tJSONL is read only during `bf sync --import` (pulling state from git) and `bf doctor --repair` (rebuilding SQLite from the artifact). Never read during normal CLI operation.\n51\t\n52\t```rust\n53\tfn import_jsonl(jsonl_path: &Path, storage: &Storage) -> Result<ImportResult> {\n54\t    let file = File::open(jsonl_path)?;\n55\t    let reader = BufReader::new(file);\n56\t    storage.with_write_transaction(|tx| {\n57\t        for line in reader.lines() {\n58\t            let issue: Issue = serde_json::from_str(&line?)?;\n59\t            tx.upsert_issue(&issue)?;\n60\t        }\n61\t        Ok(())\n62\t    })\n63\t}\n64\t```\n65\t\n66\tFunctions:\n67\t- `import_jsonl(path, storage)` — bulk upsert from JSONL into SQLite\n68\t- `stream_issues(path) -> impl Iterator<Item = Result<Issue>>` — lazy line iterator (used by import and doctor)\n69\t\n70\t### 1.3 JSONL Export (`src/jsonl.rs`)\n71\t\n72\tJSONL is written only during `bf sync --flush` (preparing the git artifact). Exports current bead state from SQLite, one entry per bead, sorted by ID for stable diffs. Atomic temp+rename.\n73\t\n74\t```rust\n75\tfn export_jsonl(jsonl_path: &Path, storage: &Storage) -> Result<ExportResult> {\n76\t    let issues = storage.list_all_issues()?;  // sorted by ID\n77\t    let temp_path = jsonl_path.with_extension(\"jsonl.tmp\");\n78\t    let mut writer = BufWriter::new(File::create_new(&temp_path)?);\n79\t    for issue in &issues {\n80\t        serde_json::to_writer(&mut writer, issue)?;\n81\t        writer.write_all(b\"\\n\")?;\n82\t    }\n83\t    writer.flush()?;\n84\t    drop(writer);\n85\t    fs::rename(&temp_path, jsonl_path)?;\n86\t    Ok(ExportResult { count: issues.len() })\n87\t}\n88\t```\n89\t\n90\tFunctions:\n91\t- `export_jsonl(path, storage)` — dump all beads from SQLite to JSONL (atomic)\n92\t- `export_jsonl_dirty(path, storage)` — export only dirty beads (incremental, faster for large workspaces)\n93\t\n94\t### 1.4 Config (`src/config.rs`)\n95\t\n96\tParse `.beads/config.yaml` with the same fields br uses:\n97\t\n98\t```yaml\n99\tissue_prefixes: [bd, fg]\n100\tdefault_priority: 2\n101\tdefault_type: task\n102\tscoring:\n103\t  priority_weight: 0.4\n104\t  blockers_weight: 0.3\n105\t  age_weight: 0.2\n106\t  labels_weight: 0.1\n107\t  max_age_hours: 20\n108\t  max_blockers: 3\n109\t# bead-forge additions (additive, br ignores these)\n110\tclaim_ttl_minutes: 30\n111\t```\n112\t\n113\tParse `.beads/metadata.json`:\n114\t```json\n115\t{ \"database\": \"beads.db\", \"jsonl_export\": \"issues.jsonl\" }\n116\t```\n117\t\n118\t### 1.5 ID Generation (`src/id.rs`)\n119\t\n120\tPort br's ID scheme: `<prefix>-<hash>` where hash is base36 lowercase. Use the birthday-problem adaptive length (3-8 chars). Read `issue_prefixes` from config (first entry is the default prefix).\n121\t\n122\t```rust\n123\tfn generate_id(prefix: &str, existing_count: usize) -> String {\n124\t    let len = optimal_hash_length(existing_count);\n125\t    let random_bytes = rand::random::<[u8; 16]>();\n126\t    let hash = sha256(&random_bytes);\n127\t    base36_encode(&hash[..len])\n128\t    format!(\"{}-{}\", prefix, hash)\n129\t}\n130\t```\n131\t\n132\t---\n133\t\n134\t## Phase 2: SQLite Primary Store\n135\t\n136\t### 2.1 Schema Application (`src/storage/schema.rs`)\n137\t\n138\tApply the exact same `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` DDL from br's `SCHEMA_SQL`. Tables:\n139\t\n140\t| Table | Purpose |\n141\t|-------|---------|\n142\t| `issues` | All 35 columns, same types, defaults, CHECK constraints |\n143\t| `dependencies` | (issue_id, depends_on_id) PK, type, metadata, thread_id |\n144\t| `labels` | (issue_id, label) PK |\n145\t| `comments` | AUTOINCREMENT id, issue_id, author, text, created_at |\n146\t| `events` | AUTOINCREMENT id, issue_id, event_type, actor, old/new/comment |\n147\t| `config` | key-value |\n148\t| `metadata` | key-value |\n149\t| `dirty_issues` | Track which issues need JSONL export |\n150\t| `export_hashes` | Incremental export tracking |\n151\t| `blocked_issues_cache` | Materialized view of blocked issues |\n152\t| `child_counters` | Hierarchical IDs (bd-abc.1, bd-abc.2) |\n153\t| `recovery_sessions` | Anomaly/recovery audit trail |\n154\t| `anomaly_audit` | Recovery event tracking |\n155\t| `bead_annotations` | bf-only: arbitrary key-value metadata per bead; separate table so br's `rebuild_issues_table()` never touches it |\n156\t\n157\tAll indexes from br must be created identically, including the critical `idx_issues_ready` composite partial index.\n158\t\n159\t### 2.2 Storage Engine (`src/storage/sqlite.rs`)\n160\t\n161\tUse `rusqlite` (not FrankenSQLite) bundled with system SQLite. Apply WAL mode, foreign keys, busy_timeout=30s, cache_size=-8000, synchronous=NORMAL.\n162\t\n163\tAll mutations go through here. JSONL is never touched during normal operation.\n164\t\n165\tFunctions:\n166\t- `open(path: &Path) -> Result<Storage>` — open/create DB, apply schema\n167\t- `get_issue(id: &str) -> Result<Option<Issue>>` — point lookup by ID\n168\t- `list_issues(filter: IssueFilter) -> Result<Vec<Issue>>` — filtered query with WHERE clauses\n169\t- `list_all_issues() -> Result<Vec<Issue>>` — full table scan sorted by ID (for JSONL export)\n170\t- `create_issue(issue: &Issue) -> Result<()>` — INSERT\n171\t- `update_issue(id: &str, changes: IssueChanges) -> Result<()>` — UPDATE + mark dirty\n172\t- `close_issue(id: &str, reason: &str) -> Result<()>` — status transition + mark dirty\n173\t- `with_write_transaction(f) -> Result<T>` — execute closure in a write transaction\n174\t- `with_immediate_transaction(f) -> Result<T>` — `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with retry (see §2.5) — acquires write lock before any reads (used by claim)\n175\t- `rebuild_blocked_cache() -> Result<()>` — recalculate blocked issues materialized view\n176\t\n177\t### 2.3 Sync Protocol (`src/sync.rs`)\n178\t\n179\tPort br's sync semantics:\n180\t\n181\t**Flush (SQLite → JSONL, for git)**:\n182\t1. Call `export_jsonl_dirty` — query dirty bead IDs, export full current state of each from SQLite\n183\t2. Atomic temp+rename over `issues.jsonl`\n184\t3. Clear `dirty_issues`, update `export_hashes`\n185\t\n186\tFor `bf sync` (full flush): call `export_jsonl` — dump all beads sorted by ID, unconditionally.\n187\t\n188\t**Import (JSONL → SQLite, from git pull)**:\n189\t1. Stream `issues.jsonl` line by line\n190\t2. Compare each with SQLite state using `content_hash`\n191\t3. INSERT new, UPDATE changed, SKIP unchanged\n192\t4. Handle collisions (same ID, different content) with deterministic resolution\n193\t\n194\t### 2.5 Concurrent Write Safety (`src/storage/sqlite.rs`)\n195\t\n196\tSQLite WAL mode serializes concurrent writers through a single write lock — they queue, not corrupt. `SQLITE_BUSY` is returned when a writer cannot acquire the lock within `busy_timeout`. With claim latency of ~1-2ms and a 20-worker fleet, the entire queue clears in ~20-40ms, so `SQLITE_BUSY` should never occur in normal operation. However, a retry wrapper is the cheap safety net that makes this a guarantee rather than an assumption:\n197\t\n198\t```rust\n199\tconst MAX_RETRIES: u32 = 5;\n200\tconst RETRY_BASE_MS: u64 = 50;\n201\t\n202\tfn with_immediate_transaction<T>(\n203\t    conn: &Connection,\n204\t    f: impl Fn(&Transaction) -> Result<T>,\n205\t) -> Result<T> {\n206\t    let mut attempt = 0;\n207\t    loop {\n208\t        match conn.execute(\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\", []) {\n209\t            Ok(_) => {\n210\t                let tx = conn.unchecked_transaction()?;\n211\t                return match f(&tx) {\n212\t                    Ok(val) => { tx.commit()?; Ok(val) }\n213\t                    Err(e) => { let _ = tx.rollback(); Err(e) }\n214\t                };\n215\t            }\n216\t            Err(e) if is_busy_error(&e) && attempt < MAX_RETRIES => {\n217\t                attempt += 1;\n218\t                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(RETRY_BASE_MS * attempt as u64));\n219\t                continue;\n220\t            }\n221\t            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n222\t        }\n223\t    }\n224\t}\n225\t\n226\tfn is_busy_error(e: &rusqlite::Error) -> bool {\n227\t    matches!(\n228\t        e,\n229\t        rusqlite::Error::SqliteFailure(\n230\t            rusqlite::ffi::Error { code: rusqlite::ErrorCode::DatabaseBusy, .. },\n231\t            _\n232\t        )\n233\t    )\n234\t}\n235\t```\n236\t\n237\t**Why this is sufficient and not a workaround**: `SQLITE_BUSY` with WAL mode is not data corruption — it is a clean \"lock unavailable, try again\" signal. The database is fully consistent when this occurs. The retry converts a transient contention spike (e.g., 20 workers all starting within the same millisecond) into a short wait rather than a user-visible error.\n238\t\n239\t**All write operations** (`claim`, `create`, `update`, `close`, `batch`) use `with_immediate_transaction`. Read-only operations (`list`, `show`, `ready`) use a plain `BEGIN DEFERRED` transaction and are never affected by write contention.\n240\t\n241\t### 2.7 Doctor/Repair (`src/doctor.rs`)\n242\t\n243\t- `doctor --repair`: Delete `beads.db`, reimport from JSONL\n244\t- `doctor --check`: Validate JSONL line integrity, check SQLite <-> JSONL consistency\n245\t- `doctor --repair --flush-first`: Flush unflushed beads to JSONL before repairing (protects against data loss)\n246\t- `doctor --repair --force`: Force repair even with unflushed beads (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\n247\t- **Flush-before-repair rule**: Always run `bf sync --flush-only` before `bf doctor --repair` to protect against losing unflushed beads\n248\t- Recovery from corruption: JSONL export is the authoritative checkpoint for recovery — `beads.db` can be rebuilt from it at any time\n249\t\n250\t**CRITICAL DATA AUTHORITY NOTE**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n251\t\n252\t| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n253\t|------|----------------|-----------------|\n254\t| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n255\t| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n256\t\n257\tThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. **Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n258\t\n259\t**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\n260\t\n261\t---\n262\t\n263\t## Phase 3: CLI Commands\n264\t\n265\t### 3.1 Command Structure (`src/cli/`)\n266\t\n267\tUse `clap` with derive macros. Binary name: `bf`. Subcommands mirror br exactly.\n268\t\n269\t```\n270\tbf create    --title \"...\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--description \"...\"] [--label ...]\n271\tbf list      [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--limit N] [--format json|text|toon]\n272\tbf show      <id>\n273\tbf update    <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>] [--title \"...\"] ...\n274\tbf close     <id> [--reason \"...\"]\n275\tbf reopen    <id>\n276\tbf delete    <id>\n277\tbf ready         [--limit N]                     # unblocked, open, sorted by priority\n278\tbf claim         --assignee <id>                 # atomic claim (see Phase 4)\n279\t                 [--model <model>]               # e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6\n280\t                 [--harness <name>]              # e.g. needle\n281\t                 [--harness-version <ver>]       # e.g. 0.5.2\n282\t                 [--workspace <path>] [--any]\n283\tbf critical-path <epic-id>                       # show critical path + float for each bead\n284\tbf dep           add-blocker <parent> <child>\n285\tbf dep           remove-blocker <parent> <child>\n286\tbf dep           tree <id>\n287\tbf label         <id> add <label>\n288\tbf label         <id> remove <label>\n289\tbf comment       <id> [--author <a>] [--text \"...\"]\n290\tbf sync          --flush-only\n291\tbf sync          --import-only\n292\tbf doctor        [--repair]\n293\tbf migrate       [<workspace>]                  # migrate br workspace to bf (see Phase 4C)\n294\t                 [--from-jsonl]                 # rebuild SQLite from JSONL + git history\n295\t                 [--seed-velocity]              # populate velocity_stats from events history\n296\t                 [--dry-run]\n297\tbf init          [--prefix <p>]\n298\tbf stats\n299\tbf count         [--status <s>]\n300\tbf search        <query>\n301\tbf schema\n302\tbf config        get <key>\n303\tbf config        set <key> <value>\n304\t```\n305\t\n306\t### 3.2 Output Formats\n307\t\n308\tThree formats, matching br exactly:\n309\t- **text**: Human-readable table (default for terminal)\n310\t- **json**: One JSON object per line (for piping)\n311\t- **toon**: Token-optimized output for LLM context windows\n312\t\n313\t### 3.3 Execution Model\n314\t\n315\tEach command:\n316\t1. Locate `.beads/` directory (walk up from CWD)\n317\t2. Load config + metadata\n318\t3. Open SQLite (`beads.db`), apply schema if new\n319\t4. Execute: mutations are SQL writes; reads are SQL queries\n320\t5. `bf sync` is the only command that touches `issues.jsonl` — flush exports it, import reads it\n321\t\n322\t### 3.4 Assignee Clearing Semantics (`--assignee \"\"` means unassigned, never an error)\n323\t\n324\t**Correct behavior (br parity):** an empty or whitespace-only `--assignee` value passed to `bf create` or `bf update` means \"no assignee\" / \"clear the assignee\" — it must never be rejected. `src/storage/sqlite.rs::update_issue` already implements this correctly:\n325\t\n326\t```rust\n327\tif let Some(ref assignee) = changes.assignee {\n328\t    if assignee.trim().is_empty() {\n329\t        // Clearing stores NULL, never an empty string that would\n330\t        // read back as \"assigned\" and hide the bead from claiming.\n331\t        updates.push(\"assignee = NULL\");\n332\t    } else {\n333\t        updates.push(\"assignee = ?\");\n334\t        params.push(Box::new(assignee.clone()));\n335\t    }\n336\t}\n337\t```\n338\t\n339\t**Known bug (currently live, blocking downstream consumers — fix tracked as bf-gj673, children bf-4mj7l and bf-2uhsk):** `src/cli/mod.rs`'s `cmd_create` and `cmd_update` both call `validate_assignee()` (`src/validation.rs`) *before* reaching the correct storage-layer logic above, and `validate_assignee()` still rejects empty/whitespace-only values with `Error: Assignee cannot be empty or whitespace-only`. This means the correct clear-on-empty behavior is currently unreachable via the CLI — `bf update <id> --assignee \"\"` fails outright instead of clearing the field.\n340\t\n341\t- `validate_assignee()` was added by bf-2nrol (closed) per an earlier, since-superseded design (\"assignee must be non-empty when provided\"). The storage layer was later fixed for `update`'s NULL-on-empty semantics without removing this now-contradictory CLI guard.\n342\t- `tests/test_assignee_validation.rs` already documents the intended fix: 6 tests are marked `#[ignore = \"aspirational: assignee validation never implemented; empty assignee now means clear/unassigned (br parity) - revisit via tracking bead\"]` — asserting the *old* (wrong) rejection behavior. These need to be rewritten to assert the *correct* behavior (success + assignee cleared/unset) once the CLI guard is removed.\n343\t- `cmd_create` has a second, independent gap: even after the CLI guard is removed, it assigns `issue.assignee = assignee` directly (`src/cli/mod.rs` around line 1104) with no empty-to-`None` normalization — unlike `update_issue`, which explicitly avoids ever storing a literal empty string. `bf create --assignee \"\"` must create a bead with `assignee = NULL`, not `assignee = \"\"` (an empty string would read back as \"assigned\" and hide the bead from claiming — the same failure mode the storage-layer comment above already guards against for `update`).\n344\t- **`bf reopen` (`cmd_reopen`) has a separate, related bug**: it only ever sets `status: Some(Status::Open)` in `IssueChanges`, leaving `assignee: None` (`IssueChanges`'s default = \"don't touch\"). A bead reopened after being closed/tombstoned therefore keeps whatever assignee it had before — a reopened bead should always come back unassigned. This is confirmed as the root cause of a real production incident (see below): beads reopened by a fleet worker retained a stale foreign assignee, which permanently hid them from that worker fleet's candidate discovery (any bead with a non-empty assignee is treated as already-claimed) even though `status` correctly read `open`.\n345\t\n346\t**Why this matters — real-world impact:** NEEDLE (the primary consumer of `bf` as a fleet worker) relies on exactly this \"empty assignee clears it\" contract in two places: its bead-release-on-failure/timeout path (`bf update <id> --status open --assignee \"\"`) and a newer self-healing mend step (`clear_assignee()`, which calls `bf update <id> --assignee \"\"`) that's specifically designed to recover beads left with a stale assignee after a `reopen`. Both currently fail against `bf`, and — because `bf reopen` doesn't clear `assignee` either — beads reopened by any tool got stuck in a state (`open` + non-empty assignee) that no NEEDLE self-healing path can currently recover from. Traced end-to-end during a 2026-07-21 lab fleet audit ([[project_needle_lab_test_pollution_2026-07-21]] in that session's memory) — this was the actual root cause of several idle NEEDLE roaming workers permanently excluding real ready work.\n347\t\n348\t---\n349\t\n350\t## Phase 4: Concurrent Claiming\n351\t\n352\t### 4.1 Architecture: SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`\n353\t\n354\tThe thundering herd problem — N workers racing to claim the same bead — is solved by running the entire read-score-update sequence inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. SQLite's write lock is acquired before any reads, so no two workers can read the same candidate state. No flock, no server, no daemon.\n355\t\n356\t```\n357\tWorker 1: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → SELECT candidates → score → UPDATE winner → COMMIT\n358\tWorker 2: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked at write lock until Worker 1 COMMITs) → SELECT → score → UPDATE → COMMIT\n359\tWorker 3: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked) → ...\n360\t...\n361\tWorker 20: BEGIN IMMEDIATE → (blocked) → SELECT → NONE (queue empty) → COMMIT (no-op)\n362\t```\n363\t\n364\tEach claim is a single CLI invocation. The critical section (lock held) is: SELECT scoring fields → score in memory → UPDATE winner + stale resets → COMMIT. Lock held for ~0.5-2ms.\n365\t\n366\t**Throughput**: SQLite handles claims purely in memory after the initial page cache warm-up:\n367\t\n368\t| Workspace | Active beads | Claim latency | Throughput |\n369\t|-----------|-------------|---------------|-----------|\n370\t| Typical (FORGE) | 248 | ~0.5ms | ~2000/sec |\n371\t| Medium (NEEDLE) | 518 | ~1ms | ~1000/sec |\n372\t| Large | 2000 | ~2ms | ~500/sec |\n373\t\n374\tWith 20 workers claiming simultaneously, the last worker waits ~20-40ms (19 queued transactions × ~1-2ms each). The fleet needs ~1-2 claims/sec at steady state — SQLite is overkill by 3 orders of magnitude.\n375\t\n376\t### 4.2 Atomic Claim (`src/claim.rs`)\n377\t\n378\tThe entire claim sequence runs inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. SQLite acquires the write lock before any reads, so no two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n379\t\n380\t```rust\n381\tfn claim(storage: &Storage, worker: &str, claim_ttl: Duration) -> Result<Option<Issue>> {\n382\t    storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n383\t        let now = Utc::now();\n384\t\n385\t        // 1. Reclaim stale in_progress beads\n386\t        tx.execute(\n387\t            \"UPDATE issues SET status='open', assignee=NULL, updated_at=?1\n388\t             WHERE status='in_progress' AND updated_at < ?2\",\n389\t            params![now, now - claim_ttl],\n390\t        )?;\n391\t\n392\t        // 2. Load scoring fields for open, unblocked candidates\n393\t        //    (blocked_issues_cache is a materialized view maintained on dep changes)\n394\t        let candidates: Vec<ScoreEntry> = tx.query_map(\n395\t            \"SELECT id, priority, updated_at,\n396\t                    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dependencies d\n397\t                     JOIN issues b ON b.id = d.depends_on_id\n398\t                     WHERE d.issue_id IN (\n399\t                         SELECT issue_id FROM dependencies\n400\t                         WHERE depends_on_id = issues.id AND type='blocks'\n401\t                     ) AND b.status = 'open') AS downstream_impact\n402\t             FROM issues\n403\t             WHERE status = 'open'\n404\t               AND id NOT IN (SELECT issue_id FROM blocked_issues_cache)\n405\t             ORDER BY downstream_impact DESC, priority ASC, created_at ASC\",\n406\t            [],\n407\t            |row| ScoreEntry::from_row(row),\n408\t        )?;\n409\t\n410\t        if candidates.is_empty() {\n411\t            return Ok(None);\n412\t        }\n413\t\n414\t        // 3. Claim the top candidate\n415\t        let winner = &candidates[0];\n416\t        tx.execute(\n417\t            \"UPDATE issues SET status='in_progress', assignee=?1, updated_at=?2\n418\t             WHERE id=?3\",\n419\t            params![worker, now, winner.id],\n420\t        )?;\n421\t        tx.execute(\n422\t            \"INSERT INTO events (issue_id, event_type, actor, old_value, new_value, created_at)\n423\t             VALUES (?1, 'claimed', ?2, 'open', 'in_progress', ?3)\",\n424\t            params![winner.id, worker, now],\n425\t        )?;\n426\t        tx.mark_dirty(&winner.id)?;\n427\t\n428\t        Ok(Some(tx.get_issue(&winner.id)?))\n429\t    })\n430\t}\n431\t```\n432\t\n433\t**Key properties**:\n434\t- **Correctness**: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` holds the SQLite write lock for the entire read-score-update sequence. No two workers can observe the same candidate state.\n435\t- **Crash safety**: If the process crashes mid-transaction, SQLite rolls back automatically. No partial state is committed.\n436\t- **Stale reclamation is a side effect**: The first statement in every claim resets expired `in_progress` beads before scoring. No separate process.\n437\t- **Impact-weighted scoring**: The query orders by `downstream_impact` (beads that would unblock the most work) then priority, then FIFO.\n438\t- **No flock, no file I/O**: The entire claim is in-memory SQL execution after page cache warm-up. `issues.jsonl` is not touched.\n439\t\n440\t### 4.3 Multi-Workspace Claiming (`src/claim.rs`)\n441\t\n442\tFor `bf claim --any` (claim from any workspace), open each workspace's SQLite, run the scoring query on each, pick the global winner, claim it:\n443\t\n444\t```rust\n445\tfn claim_any(workspace_paths: &[PathBuf], worker: &str, claim_ttl: Duration) -> Result<Option<Issue>> {\n446\t    // Score across all workspaces — each Storage::open is cheap (WAL, page cache)\n447\t    let mut best: Option<(Score, PathBuf)> = None;\n448\t    for path in workspace_paths {\n449\t        let storage = Storage::open(&path.join(\".beads/beads.db\"))?;\n450\t        if let Some(score) = storage.top_candidate_score(claim_ttl)? {\n451\t            if best.as_ref().map(|(b, _)| score > *b).unwrap_or(true) {\n452\t                best = Some((score, path.clone()));\n453\t            }\n454\t        }\n455\t    }\n456\t\n457\t    match best {\n458\t        None => Ok(None),\n459\t        Some((_, path)) => {\n460\t            let storage = Storage::open(&path.join(\".beads/beads.db\"))?;\n461\t            claim(&storage, worker, claim_ttl)\n462\t        }\n463\t    }\n464\t}\n465\t```\n466\t\n467\tNo cross-workspace locking needed — each `claim()` call uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on its own SQLite file. Two workers racing on the same workspace are serialized by SQLite; two workers racing on different workspaces proceed in parallel.\n468\t\n469\t### 4.4 Stale Claim Detection\n470\t\n471\tNo background process needed. Stale detection runs as part of every `bf claim` invocation:\n472\t\n473\t1. Inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`: `UPDATE issues SET status='open' WHERE status='in_progress' AND updated_at < now - claim_ttl`\n474\t2. This runs before candidate scoring — stale beads become eligible again in the same transaction\n475\t3. Single SQL statement, no extra I/O\n476\t\n477\t**Claim TTL**: Default 30 minutes, configurable in `.beads/config.yaml`:\n478\t\n479\t```yaml\n480\tclaim_ttl_minutes: 30\n481\t```\n482\t\n483\t**TTL tuning**: With 20 workers and tasks taking 5-15 minutes, 30 minutes is conservative. A worker that's actively working but slow will have its bead remain `in_progress` — stale reclamation only triggers if the worker hasn't updated the bead in 30 minutes. Since the worker closes the bead when done (writing a new entry), active workers never get reclaimed.\n484\t\n485\t**Manual stale scan**: For workspaces with no active claiming (no fleet running), `bf doctor --reclaim-stale` performs the same scan without claiming a bead. Can be run via cron for long-running workspaces with occasional stuck claims.\n486\t\n487\t### 4.5 CLI Usage\n488\t\n489\t```bash\n490\t# Claim from current workspace\n491\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 --json\n492\t\n493\t# Claim with worker metadata (feeds velocity-aware scoring — see §4B.6)\n494\tbf claim --assignee worker-7 \\\n495\t         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n496\t         --harness needle \\\n497\t         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n498\t         --json\n499\t\n500\t# Claim from a specific workspace\n501\tbf claim --workspace containers/zai-proxy/ --assignee worker-3 --json\n502\t\n503\t# Claim highest priority across all workspaces\n504\tbf claim --any --assignee worker-12 --json\n505\t\n506\t# Prefer a workspace, fall back to any\n507\tbf claim --workspace containers/zai-proxy/ --fallback any --assignee worker-5 --json\n508\t```\n509\t\n510\tAll commands work identically in all modes — no server required, no daemon running. Each `bf claim` is a self-contained CLI invocation: lock, read, claim, write, unlock, exit.\n511\t\n512\tWorker metadata (`--model`, `--harness`, `--harness-version`) is stored in the claim event row and the `worker_sessions` table. It drives velocity-aware scoring (§4B.6) and appears in `bf log` output so you can see exactly which model/harness combination claimed each bead.\n513\t\n514\t### 4.6 Why No Server\n515\t\n516\tThe plan originally included a coordination server with `Arc<Mutex<ServerState>>`, in-memory priority queues, heartbeats, and a Unix socket protocol. This was removed because:\n517\t\n518\t1. **SQLite is sufficient**: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` provides serialized write access. Claim latency is ~0.5-2ms — 4-16× faster than the previous flock+streaming-rewrite approach.\n519\t2. **Simpler operations**: No flock infrastructure, no streaming rewrite, no temp files during normal operation. All mutation logic is SQL.\n520\t3. **Crash recovery is automatic**: SQLite rolls back incomplete transactions on next open. No partial state, no temp file cleanup.\n521\t4. **Real-world scale validates it**: A 2,000-bead workspace takes ~2ms per claim. A 20-worker fleet needs ~1-2 claims/sec. SQLite delivers ~500 claims/sec at that size.\n522\t5. **Server is a future optimization**: A persistent in-memory server would reduce per-claim latency from ~2ms to ~0.1ms by eliminating SQLite file I/O entirely. Premature for current scale — can be added transparently later.\n523\t\n524\t### 4.7 Comparison to br's Race Condition\n525\t\n526\t| Scenario | br (beads_rust) | bf (bead-forge) |\n527\t|----------|-----------------|-----------------|\n528\t| 20 workers claim simultaneously | 20 read same JSONL, all see same \"next\" bead, all write `in_progress` — last writer wins, 19 workers have phantom claims | 20 workers serialized by SQLite write lock — each BEGIN IMMEDIATE sees post-commit state, each gets a distinct bead |\n529\t| Worker crashes mid-claim | N/A (no lock) | SQLite rolls back the incomplete transaction automatically on next open |\n530\t| Stale claim (worker died) | Bead stays `in_progress` forever | Next claim invocation reclaims beads older than TTL |\n531\t| Cross-workspace claiming | Not supported | `--any` locks all JSONL files in sorted order |\n532\t\n533\t---\n534\t\n535\t## Phase 4B: Extended Features\n536\t\n537\t### 4B.1 JSONL Rotation (`src/rotate.rs`)\n538\t\n539\tKeep `issues.jsonl` lean for fast claiming. With one entry per bead, the file grows only when new beads are created — but over a long project lifetime the accumulation of closed beads still grows the file. Rotation evicts closed beads into numbered archive files, keeping the active scan set small.\n540\t\n541\t```\n542\t.beads/\n543\t├── issues.jsonl          # active: open, in_progress, blocked, deferred + recently closed\n544\t├── issues.jsonl.1        # archive: closed beads rotated out most recently\n545\t├── issues.jsonl.2        # archive: older closed beads\n546\t└── issues.jsonl.3        # archive: oldest\n547\t```\n548\t\n549\t**Rotation rules**:\n550\t- `bf rotate` moves closed beads older than `rotate_age_days` (default 30) from `issues.jsonl` into `issues.jsonl.1` via streaming rewrite (active file) + streaming append (archive file)\n551\t- When `issues.jsonl.1` exceeds `rotate_max_size` (default 5MB), it becomes `issues.jsonl.2`, `.2` → `.3`, etc.\n552\t- Maximum archive files: `rotate_max_archives` (default 5). Oldest archive is deleted.\n553\t\n554\t**Claim only reads the active file**. This keeps claim latency proportional to the number of active (non-closed) beads rather than total workspace history.\n555\t\n556\t**Reading archived beads**: `bf show <id>` searches the active file first, then archives. `bf list --all` includes archives. `bf log <id>` searches all files for the full history.\n557\t\n558\t**git integration**: `.beads/issues.jsonl` is committed to git. Archive files (`.jsonl.1`, `.2`, ...) are also committed — they're part of the project history. The `.beads/` directory is the bead store and should be version-controlled alongside the code.\n559\t\n560\t**Secret protection**: Before any write, bf scans bead fields for secret patterns (AWS keys, private keys, API tokens, passwords) using a built-in regex set similar to git-secrets. If a match is found:\n561\t- `bf create` / `bf update` prints a warning and refuses the write\n562\t- `bf commit-check` (git pre-commit hook) scans staged changes to `.beads/` for secrets\n563\t- Patterns are configurable in `.beads/config.yaml`:\n564\t\n565\t```yaml\n566\tsecret_protection:\n567\t  enabled: true\n568\t  # Additional patterns (matched against all string fields)\n569\t  deny_patterns:\n570\t    - \"-----BEGIN (RSA |EC |DSA )?PRIVATE KEY-----\"\n571\t    - \"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\"          # AWS access key\n572\t    - \"sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{32,}\"       # OpenAI/Anthropic API key\n573\t  # Fields to exclude from scanning (e.g., known test values)\n574\t  allowlist_fields: []\n575\t```\n576\t\n577\tConfig:\n578\t\n579\t```yaml\n580\trotate_age_days: 30\n581\trotate_max_size_mb: 5\n582\trotate_max_archives: 5\n583\t```\n584\t\n585\t### 4B.2 Batch Operations (`src/batch.rs`)\n586\t\n587\tExecute multiple operations atomically under a single SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. Replaces sequences of N separate CLI invocations with one.\n588\t\n589\t```bash\n590\t# From a file\n591\tbf batch --file operations.json\n592\t\n593\t# From stdin (one operation per line)\n594\techo 'create --title \"child 1\" --type task\n595\tcreate --title \"child 2\" --type task\n596\tdep add-blocker fg-a3f8.1 fg-a3f8\n597\tdep add-blocker fg-a3f8.2 fg-a3f8\n598\tclose fg-a3f8 --reason \"Split into children\"' | bf batch\n599\t\n600\t# Programmatic JSON input\n601\t# NEEDLE mitosis: use @0, @1 to reference created beads by position\n602\tbf batch --json '[\n603\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"child 1\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n604\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"child 2\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n605\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@0\", \"child\": \"fg-a3f8\"},\n606\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"@1\", \"child\": \"fg-a3f8\"},\n607\t  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"fg-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n608\t]'\n609\t```\n610\t\n611\t**Placeholder references**: `@0`, `@1`, etc. resolve to the IDs of beads created at that position. Critical for mitosis — you don't know child IDs until they're created.\n612\t\n613\t**Atomicity**: All operations run inside a single SQLite write transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`). If any operation fails (invalid ID, bad status transition), the transaction rolls back — no partial state is committed. Kill -9 during batch leaves the workspace in its original state.\n614\t\n615\t**Use cases**:\n616\t- NEEDLE mitosis: split 1 bead into N children (2N+1 operations → 1 batch)\n617\t- Bulk status changes: close all beads with a given label\n618\t- Migration: import beads from another tracker\n619\t- Workspace setup: create epics + child beads + dependencies in one shot\n620\t\n621\t**Output**: Returns JSON array of results, one per operation:\n622\t\n623\t```json\n624\t[\n625\t  {\"op\": 0, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"fg-b4d1\"},\n626\t  {\"op\": 1, \"status\": \"ok\", \"id\": \"fg-b4d2\"},\n627\t  {\"op\": 2, \"status\": \"ok\"},\n628\t  {\"op\": 3, \"status\": \"ok\"}\n629\t]\n630\t```\n631\t\n632\t### 4B.3 Annotations — Extensible Metadata (`src/model.rs`, `src/cli/annotate.rs`)\n633\t\n634\tArbitrary key-value pairs on any bead, stored in a **separate `bead_annotations` table** — never as a column on `issues`.\n635\t\n636\t**Why not a column on `issues`**: br's `issues_column_order_matches()` check in `schema.rs:630` fires on every `br` open and returns `false` the moment the actual column count differs from `EXPECTED_ISSUE_COLUMN_ORDER.len()`. This triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` which rewrites `issues` from br's canonical column list — destroying any bf-added columns. Adding an `annotations` column to `issues` would be silently wiped on every `br` invocation.\n637\t\n638\t**Schema** (br never touches this table):\n639\t\n640\t```sql\n641\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bead_annotations (\n642\t    bead_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n643\t    key     TEXT NOT NULL,\n644\t    value   TEXT NOT NULL,\n645\t    PRIMARY KEY (bead_id, key)\n646\t);\n647\tCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bead_annotations_key_value\n648\t    ON bead_annotations (key, value);  -- for bf list --annotation key=value\n649\t```\n650\t\n651\t**Issue struct** (annotations loaded via JOIN, serialized into the JSONL field):\n652\t\n653\t```rust\n654\t#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = \"BTreeMap::is_empty\")]\n655\tpub annotations: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n656\t```\n657\t\n658\tJSONL export serializes annotations into the `Issue` JSON object. On import, annotations are upserted into `bead_annotations`. br ignores the `annotations` JSON field when reading JSONL (`skip_unknown_fields`), so JSONL round-trips are clean.\n659\t\n660\t**CLI**:\n661\t\n662\t```bash\n663\t# Set annotations\n664\tbf annotate fg-a3f8 needle_attempt=3 needle_session=abc123\n665\tbf annotate fg-a3f8 review_status=needs_review\n666\t\n667\t# Remove annotations\n668\tbf annotate fg-a3f8 --remove needle_error\n669\t\n670\t# Query by annotation\n671\tbf list --annotation needle_attempt=3\n672\tbf list --annotation review_status=needs_review\n673\t\n674\t# Show annotations (included in bf show output)\n675\tbf show fg-a3f8 --json | jq '.annotations'\n676\t```\n677\t\n678\t**br backward compatibility**: br never reads, writes, or rebuilds `bead_annotations`. When br opens a bf-migrated database: its `issues_column_order_matches()` check passes (no extra columns on `issues`), no rebuild fires, annotation data is untouched. When br creates a bead, `bead_annotations` has no row for it — that is correct, the bead just has no annotations yet.\n679\t\n680\t**Use cases**:\n681\t- NEEDLE: `needle_attempt`, `needle_session`, `needle_error`, `needle_worker_version`\n682\t- Custom tools: `ci_build_id`, `deployment_sha`, `jira_key`\n683\t- Fleet tracking: `claimed_at`, `heartbeat_at`, `estimated_minutes_remaining`\n684\t\n685\t### 4B.4 Operation History — `bf log` (`src/log.rs`)\n686\t\n687\tShow the history of mutations on a specific bead or workspace, sourced from the SQLite events table and git history.\n688\t\n689\t```bash\n690\tbf log fg-a3f8                          # full history of this bead\n691\tbf log --since \"2026-04-25\"             # all workspace changes since date\n692\tbf log --actor worker-3                 # changes by a specific worker\n693\tbf log --limit 20                       # last 20 mutations\n694\tbf log --status-changes                 # only status transitions\n695\t```\n696\t\n697\tOutput:\n698\t\n699\t```\n700\t2026-04-25 10:00  CREATED     by: human        \"Implement auth flow\"\n701\t2026-04-25 10:05  DEP_ADD     by: human        blocked by fg-b2c1\n702\t2026-04-25 14:30  CLAIMED     by: worker-3     status: open → in_progress\n703\t2026-04-25 15:45  COMMENT     by: worker-3     \"Found edge case in token refresh\"\n704\t2026-04-25 16:00  CLOSED      by: worker-3     \"Completed\"\n705\t```\n706\t\n707\t**Implementation**: History is sourced from two places:\n708\t\n709\t1. **SQLite events table** (primary): every mutation records an event row (`event_type`, `actor`, `old_value`, `new_value`). `bf log` queries this table directly — O(1) lookup by issue ID, no file scanning.\n710\t\n711\t2. **Git history** (fallback/deep history): `issues.jsonl` is committed to git on each sync. `git log -p .beads/issues.jsonl` shows every past state of the file. `bf log --git` uses this for history older than the events table retention window.\n712\t\n713\tSince JSONL has one entry per bead (not a mutation log), JSONL diffing is not used for history. The events table is the authoritative mutation record.\n714\t\n715\t**`bf log --diff`**: Show the field-level diff from the events table:\n716\t\n717\t```bash\n718\tbf log fg-a3f8 --diff\n719\t# 2026-04-25 14:30  CLAIMED\n720\t#   - status: \"open\" → \"in_progress\"\n721\t#   + assignee: null → \"worker-3\"\n722\t#   + annotations.needle_attempt: \"1\" → \"2\"\n723\t```\n724\t\n725\t### 4B.5 Critical Path Computation (`src/critical_path.rs`)\n726\t\n727\tComputes the longest dependency chain through the workspace graph and annotates each bead with its **float** — how many hops it can slip before delaying the epic. Beads with `float == 0` are on the critical path; every day they're blocked delays completion by a day.\n728\t\n729\t**Command**:\n730\t\n731\t```bash\n732\t$ bf critical-path fg-epic-auth\n733\t\n734\tCritical path for fg-epic-auth (14 open beads, 3 on critical path):\n735\t\n736\t  float=0  [fg-a3f8] Implement auth token refresh        in_progress (worker-3)\n737\t  float=0  [fg-b2c1] Fix concurrent session state bug    open\n738\t  float=0  [fg-c4d9] Integration tests: auth flow        open\n739\t  float=2  [fg-d5e3] Update API documentation            open\n740\t  float=2  [fg-e6f4] Refactor error response format      open\n741\t  float=5  [fg-f7g5] Add rate limiting headers           open\n742\t  ...\n743\t\n744\tLongest chain: fg-a3f8 → fg-b2c1 → fg-c4d9 → [epic closes]\n745\tMinimum remaining time: 3 bead-completions on critical path\n746\t```\n747\t\n748\t**Algorithm**: Two-pass walk on the dependency DAG using SQLite recursive CTEs.\n749\t\n750\tPass 1 (forward — compute earliest start `ES`): start from beads with no open predecessors (`ES=0`). For each bead, `ES = max(ES of all open predecessors) + 1`.\n751\t\n752\tPass 2 (backward — compute latest start `LS`): start from the epic. For each bead, `LS = min(LS of all successors) - 1`. `float = LS - ES`. Zero-float beads form the critical path.\n753\t\n754\t```sql\n755\tWITH RECURSIVE\n756\t  -- Forward pass: earliest start for each open bead\n757\t  forward(id, es) AS (\n758\t    SELECT i.id, 0\n759\t    FROM issues i\n760\t    WHERE i.status IN ('open', 'in_progress')\n761\t      AND NOT EXISTS (\n762\t        SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d\n763\t        JOIN issues pred ON pred.id = d.depends_on_id\n764\t        WHERE d.issue_id = i.id AND d.type = 'blocks'\n765\t          AND pred.status IN ('open', 'in_progress')\n766\t      )\n767\t    UNION ALL\n768\t    SELECT d.issue_id, MAX(f.es) + 1\n769\t    FROM dependencies d\n770\t    JOIN forward f ON f.id = d.depends_on_id\n771\t    WHERE d.type = 'blocks'\n772\t    GROUP BY d.issue_id\n773\t  )\n774\tSELECT id, es,\n775\t       (SELECT MAX(es) FROM forward) - es AS float\n776\tFROM forward\n777\tORDER BY float ASC, es ASC;\n778\t```\n779\t\n780\t**Schema addition**: `critical_path_cache` table — recomputed whenever a dependency is added/removed or a bead changes status. Invalidated by a trigger on `dependencies` and `issues.status`.\n781\t\n782\t```sql\n783\tCREATE TABLE critical_path_cache (\n784\t    bead_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES issues(id),\n785\t    epic_id     TEXT REFERENCES issues(id),\n786\t    es          INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- earliest start (hops from root)\n787\t    ls          INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- latest start\n788\t    float       INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- ls - es; 0 = critical path\n789\t    updated_at  DATETIME NOT NULL\n790\t);\n791\t```\n792\t\n793\t**Integration with claim scoring**: The claim query joins `critical_path_cache` and adds a large bonus for zero-float beads:\n794\t\n795\t```sql\n796\t1000.0 / (COALESCE(cp.float, 999) + 1) AS critical_path_bonus\n797\t```\n798\t\n799\tA zero-float bead gets `1000 / 1 = 1000` bonus. A float-5 bead gets `1000 / 6 ≈ 167`. A bead not on any epic path gets `1000 / 1000 = 1`. This ensures critical-path beads always sort above non-critical beads regardless of their listed priority.\n800\t\n801\t**`bf dep add-blocker` side effect**: Every time a dependency is created or removed, the cache for the affected epic is invalidated and recomputed inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. Recompute cost is O(V + E) — for a 500-bead workspace with 300 deps, under 1ms.\n802\t\n803\t### 4B.6 Velocity-Aware Impact Scoring (`src/velocity.rs`)\n804\t\n805\tThe claim scorer currently orders by `downstream_impact / priority`. That's correct for maximizing throughput when all workers and task types take similar time. In practice, a `claude-opus-4-7` worker closes `bug` beads in 8 minutes while the same harness on `claude-haiku-4-5` takes 35 minutes for the same type — a 4× difference. The optimal claim for each worker is the task where `impact / expected_duration` is maximized for *that specific worker configuration*, not the global impact rank.\n806\t\n807\t**Worker metadata on claim**: Workers pass their composition to `bf claim`:\n808\t\n809\t```bash\n810\tbf claim --assignee worker-01 \\\n811\t         --model claude-sonnet-4-6 \\\n812\t         --harness needle \\\n813\t         --harness-version 0.5.2 \\\n814\t         --json\n815\t```\n816\t\n817\t**Schema**:\n818\t\n819\t```sql\n820\t-- One row per worker session (created on bf claim, updated on bf close)\n821\tCREATE TABLE worker_sessions (\n822\t    session_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  -- UUID generated by worker\n823\t    worker_id       TEXT NOT NULL,\n824\t    model           TEXT,              -- 'claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-opus-4-7', etc.\n825\t    harness         TEXT,              -- 'needle', 'custom'\n826\t    harness_version TEXT,              -- '0.5.2'\n827\t    bead_id         TEXT REFERENCES issues(id),\n828\t    claimed_at      DATETIME,\n829\t    closed_at       DATETIME,\n830\t    duration_seconds INTEGER           -- populated on bf close\n831\t);\n832\t\n833\t-- Aggregated velocity statistics per (model, harness, issue_type)\n834\tCREATE TABLE velocity_stats (\n835\t    model           TEXT NOT NULL,\n836\t    harness         TEXT NOT NULL,\n837\t    issue_type      TEXT NOT NULL,\n838\t    sample_count    INTEGER DEFAULT 0,\n839\t    p50_seconds     INTEGER,\n840\t    p90_seconds     INTEGER,\n841\t    avg_seconds     REAL,\n842\t    last_updated    DATETIME,\n843\t    PRIMARY KEY (model, harness, issue_type)\n844\t);\n845\t```\n846\t\n847\t**Update on close**: When `bf close <id>` is called, if the closing worker passed `--session-id <uuid>`, the session row is updated with `closed_at` and `duration_seconds`. A trigger recomputes `velocity_stats` for that `(model, harness, issue_type)` tuple using a window over the last 50 sessions.\n848\t\n849\t**Claim scoring integration**: The claim query joins `velocity_stats` for the requesting worker and computes `score = impact / expected_seconds`:\n850\t\n851\t```sql\n852\tSELECT\n853\t    i.id,\n854\t    i.priority,\n855\t    i.issue_type,\n856\t    COALESCE(cp.float, 999)            AS critical_float,\n857\t    COALESCE(vs.p50_seconds, 1800)     AS expected_seconds,\n858\t    -- Combined score: more impact per unit time = higher priority\n859\t    (\n860\t      downstream_impact * 3.0\n861\t      + (4 - i.priority) * 2.0\n862\t      + 1000.0 / (COALESCE(cp.float, 999) + 1)\n863\t    ) / COALESCE(vs.p50_seconds, 1800) AS score\n864\tFROM issues i\n865\tLEFT JOIN critical_path_cache cp  ON cp.bead_id = i.id\n866\tLEFT JOIN velocity_stats vs       ON vs.issue_type = i.issue_type\n867\t                                 AND vs.model    = ?model\n868\t                                 AND vs.harness  = ?harness\n869\tWHERE i.status = 'open'\n870\t  AND i.id NOT IN (SELECT issue_id FROM blocked_issues_cache)\n871\tORDER BY score DESC\n872\tLIMIT 1\n873\t```\n874\t\n875\tWorkers with no velocity history use the 1800s (30-minute) default — conservative but correct. After ~10 completions per type, the estimate is meaningful.\n876\t\n877\t**`bf velocity` command**: Show the velocity table for all known worker configurations:\n878\t\n879\t```\n880\t$ bf velocity\n881\t\n882\tModel                  Harness   Type     Samples  p50    p90\n883\tclaude-opus-4-7        needle    task     142      8m     22m\n884\tclaude-opus-4-7        needle    bug      38       14m    51m\n885\tclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    task     87       18m    45m\n886\tclaude-sonnet-4-6      needle    bug      24       31m    1h12m\n887\tclaude-haiku-4-5       needle    task     23       35m    2h10m\n888\t```\n889\t\n890\tThis table surfaces which model+harness combinations are most efficient for which task types — direct input for fleet composition decisions (which models to provision for which workspace).\n891\t\n892\t**Fallback**: If `--model` is not passed to `bf claim`, the scorer uses the average across all models for that issue type. Backward compatible — undecorated `bf claim` calls work exactly as before, just without per-model scoring.\n893\t\n894\t---\n895\t\n896\t## Phase 4C: br→bf Workspace Migration (`src/migrate.rs`)\n897\t\n898\tExisting repos using `br` migrate to `bf` without data loss. Three migration paths cover all scenarios.\n899\t\n900\t### Migration Path A — Drop-in Replace (zero downtime, zero data conversion)\n901\t\n902\tThe `br`→`bf` symlink is the migration for most repos:\n903\t\n904\t```bash\n905\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n906\t```\n907\t\n908\t`apply_migrations()` in `Storage::open` handles schema differences automatically on first open:\n909\t\n910\t```rust\n911\tfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> Result<()> {\n912\t    // All bf-only tables use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS — no-op on existing DBs.\n913\t    // Annotations are stored in bead_annotations, NOT as a column on issues.\n914\t    // Reason: br's issues_column_order_matches() in schema.rs:630 fires on every\n915\t    // br open and triggers rebuild_issues_table() if the column count differs —\n916\t    // which silently destroys any extra column. bead_annotations is a separate\n917\t    // table br never reads, writes, or rebuilds.\n918\t    conn.execute_batch(\"\n919\t        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bead_annotations (\n920\t            bead_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n921\t            key     TEXT NOT NULL,\n922\t            value   TEXT NOT NULL,\n923\t            PRIMARY KEY (bead_id, key)\n924\t        );\n925\t        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bead_annotations_key_value\n926\t            ON bead_annotations (key, value);\n927\t        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS worker_sessions ( ... );\n928\t        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS velocity_stats ( ... );\n929\t        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS critical_path_cache ( ... );\n930\t    \")?;\n931\t    Ok(())\n932\t}\n933\t```\n934\t\n935\tAll bf-only tables are created with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` — the call is a no-op when the database was already created by `bf`. No column migrations on `issues` are needed.\n936\t\n937\t**br backward compatibility after migration**: `br` opens a bf-migrated database and finds the `issues` table column count matches exactly — `issues_column_order_matches()` passes, `rebuild_issues_table()` never fires. br ignores `bead_annotations`, `worker_sessions`, `velocity_stats`, and `critical_path_cache` entirely. All `br` commands (list, show, update, doctor) continue working.\n938\t\n939\t### Migration Path B — `bf migrate` (explicit, with backup and verification)\n940\t\n941\tFor workspaces where you want an audit point and rollback safety:\n942\t\n943\t```bash\n944\tbf migrate /path/to/workspace [--dry-run]\n945\t```\n946\t\n947\tSteps:\n948\t1. **Pause fleet** (optional): write a `migration_lock` row to the workspace DB so `bf claim` refuses new claims during migration\n949\t2. **Backup**: `cp beads.db beads.db.br-backup-<timestamp>`\n950\t3. **Apply migrations**: call `apply_migrations()` explicitly\n951\t4. **Prime caches**: populate `critical_path_cache` for all epics in one pass\n952\t5. **Seed config**: add `bf`-specific keys with defaults to `config.yaml` if absent:\n953\t   ```yaml\n954\t   # bead-forge additions (br ignores these)\n955\t   claim_ttl_minutes: 30\n956\t   rotate_age_days: 30\n957\t   rotate_max_size_mb: 5\n958\t   ```\n959\t6. **Verify forward compat**: run `br doctor --db beads.db` — must exit 0\n960\t7. **Verify backward compat**: run `bf doctor --check` — must exit 0\n961\t8. **Release fleet**: remove `migration_lock`\n962\t\n963\tOutput:\n964\t```\n965\tMigrating /home/coding/FORGE/.beads\n966\t  ✓ Backed up beads.db → beads.db.br-backup-2026-04-30T09:15:00Z\n967\t  ✓ Applied schema migrations (created bead_annotations, worker_sessions, velocity_stats, critical_path_cache tables)\n968\t  ✓ Primed critical_path_cache for 3 epics (247 beads)\n969\t  ✓ Updated config.yaml with bf defaults\n970\t  ✓ br doctor: OK\n971\t  ✓ bf doctor: OK\n972\tMigration complete. br symlink: ln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n973\t```\n974\t\n975\t### Migration Path C — `bf migrate --from-jsonl` (events table lost)\n976\t\n977\tWhen `beads.db` is missing or corrupted beyond repair and only `issues.jsonl` is available (the `br doctor --repair` scenario). The standard reimport loses the `events` table — all claim/close history vanishes.\n978\t\n979\t`--from-jsonl` recovers history from git:\n980\t\n981\t```bash\n982\tbf migrate /path/to/workspace --from-jsonl [--seed-velocity]\n983\t```\n984\t\n985\t1. **Reimport**: stream `issues.jsonl` into fresh SQLite (standard import)\n986\t2. **Reconstruct events from git log**:\n987\t   ```bash\n988\t   git log --follow -p .beads/issues.jsonl\n989\t   ```\n990\t   For each commit that touched `issues.jsonl`:\n991\t   - Diff the JSONL before/after\n992\t   - New bead appearing → synthetic `created` event with commit timestamp + author\n993\t   - Bead status changing `open→in_progress` → synthetic `claimed` event\n994\t   - Bead status changing `in_progress→closed` → synthetic `closed` event + compute `duration_seconds`\n995\t   - Synthetic events get `metadata: {\"source\": \"git-reconstructed\", \"commit\": \"<sha>\"}`\n996\t3. **Seed velocity stats** (`--seed-velocity`): from reconstructed `closed` events with known actor, compute `(model=unknown, harness=unknown, issue_type)` averages. Actor name patterns (`worker-claude-sonnet-4-6-01`) can infer model if the naming convention was consistent.\n997\t\n998\tRecovery completeness depends on how often `bf sync` was run (each sync = one JSONL commit in git). With daily syncs: ~95% of events reconstructed. With hourly syncs: ~99%.\n999\t\n1000\t### Migration Checklist for All Repos\n1001\t\n1002\t```bash\n1003\t# Per-machine: install bf, symlink br\n1004\tcurl -L https://github.com/jedarden/bead-forge/releases/latest/download/bf-linux-x86_64 \\\n1005\t  -o ~/.local/bin/bf && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/bf\n1006\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n1007\t\n1008\t# Per-workspace: explicit migration with backup\n1009\tfor workspace in \\\n1010\t  /home/coding/FORGE \\\n1011\t  /home/coding/NEEDLE \\\n1012\t  /home/coding/AgentScribe \\\n1013\t  /home/coding/ARMOR \\\n1014\t  /home/coding/SIGIL \\\n1015\t  /home/coding/CLASP \\\n1016\t  /home/coding/bead-forge; do\n1017\t  bf migrate \"$workspace\"\n1018\tdone\n1019\t\n1020\t# Update NEEDLE config to pass worker metadata\n1021\t# In .config/needle/adapters/claude-sonnet.yaml, add to invoke_template:\n1022\t#   bf claim --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --harness needle --harness-version 0.5.2 ...\n1023\t```\n1024\t\n1025\t### Schema Compatibility Matrix\n1026\t\n1027\t| Scenario | br behavior | Result |\n1028\t|----------|-------------|--------|\n1029\t| br opens bf-created DB | `issues` column count matches br's expected count exactly (no extra columns); br ignores `bead_annotations`, `worker_sessions`, `velocity_stats`, `critical_path_cache` | ✓ Full compat |\n1030\t| bf opens br-created DB | `apply_migrations()` creates `bead_annotations` + bf-only tables via `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` | ✓ Transparent |\n1031\t| bf opens very old br DB (missing `issues` columns) | br's own `rebuild_issues_table()` handles this on next `br` open; bf schema also applies its own `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for bf-only tables | ✓ Handled |\n1032\t| br and bf open same DB concurrently | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent; WAL serializes writes | ✓ Safe |\n1033\t| bf opens bf-created DB | `apply_migrations()` is no-op — all tables already exist | ✓ Idempotent |\n1034\t\n1035\t---\n1036\t\n1037\t## Phase 5: NEEDLE Integration\n1038\t\n1039\tNEEDLE's `bead_store/mod.rs` chains several `br` CLI calls that have race windows between them. Each race is eliminated by the corresponding `bf` command.\n1040\t\n1041\t### 5.1 Race 1 — `claim()`: two-process verify (lines 518-558)\n1042\t\n1043\t**br (racy)**:\n1044\t```rust\n1045\t// Call 1: br update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <actor>\n1046\t// ← race window: another worker sees this bead as open and claims it ←\n1047\t// Call 2: br show <id>  (to verify .assignee == actor)\n1048\t```\n1049\tTwo processes, two SQLite opens. If two workers race, both issue `br update` and `br` does not enforce exclusivity — it just overwrites. The `br show` verify is too late: the wrong worker may have overwritten the `assignee` field between the two calls.\n1050\t\n1051\t**bf (atomic)**:\n1052\t```bash\n1053\tbead=$(bf claim --workspace \"$WORKSPACE\" --assignee \"$WORKER\" --json)\n1054\t```\n1055\t`bf claim` runs the full read-score-update sequence inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. No second call, no verify step needed.\n1056\t\n1057\t### 5.2 Race 2 — `ready()` → `claim()`: TOCTOU (lines 487-507)\n1058\t\n1059\t**br (racy)**:\n1060\t```rust\n1061\t// Call 1: br ready --json  → returns candidate list (a snapshot)\n1062\t// ← race window: another worker claims the top candidate ←\n1063\t// Call 2: claim(selected_id)  → may be claiming an already-claimed bead\n1064\t```\n1065\tThe winning bead is selected from a stale snapshot. By the time `claim()` issues `br update`, the bead may have been claimed by another worker.\n1066\t\n1067\t**bf (atomic)**:\n1068\t```bash\n1069\tbead=$(bf claim --workspace \"$WORKSPACE\" --assignee \"$WORKER\" --json)\n1070\t```\n1071\tScoring and claiming happen inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. The candidate list is read and the winner is updated atomically — no snapshot staleness.\n1072\t\n1073\t### 5.3 Race 3 — Mitosis: `create_bead` + `add_dependency` (lines 607-639)\n1074\t\n1075\t**br (non-atomic)**:\n1076\t```rust\n1077\t// Call 1: br create \"child title\"  → returns new bead ID\n1078\t// ← process crash here → orphaned bead with no dependency link ←\n1079\t// Call 2: br dep add <parent_id> <child_id>\n1080\t```\n1081\tIf NEEDLE dies between `br create` and `br dep add`, the child bead exists but is not linked to the parent. The parent is never closed; the orphaned child is never picked up.\n1082\t\n1083\t**bf (atomic)**:\n1084\t```bash\n1085\tbf batch --json '[\n1086\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"child 1\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n1087\t  {\"op\": \"create\", \"title\": \"child 2\", \"type\": \"task\"},\n1088\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"fg-a3f8.1\", \"child\": \"fg-a3f8\"},\n1089\t  {\"op\": \"dep_add_blocker\", \"parent\": \"fg-a3f8.2\", \"child\": \"fg-a3f8\"},\n1090\t  {\"op\": \"close\", \"id\": \"fg-a3f8\", \"reason\": \"Split into children\"}\n1091\t]'\n1092\t```\n1093\tAll five operations run inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. If NEEDLE dies mid-batch, the transaction rolls back automatically — no partial state.\n1094\t\n1095\t### 5.4 Inefficiency — `labels()` round-trip (lines 584-588)\n1096\t\n1097\t**br (wasteful)**:\n1098\t```rust\n1099\tasync fn labels(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n1100\t    let bead = self.show(id).await?;  // full br show just to get .labels\n1101\t    Ok(bead.labels)\n1102\t}\n1103\t```\n1104\tOne full `br show` (with JSON deserialization of all 35 fields) to extract one field.\n1105\t\n1106\t**bf (direct)**:\n1107\t```bash\n1108\tbf labels <id> --json   # SELECT label FROM labels WHERE issue_id = ?\n1109\t```\n1110\tDirect `SELECT` on the `labels` table. Single column, single round-trip.\n1111\t\n1112\t### 5.5 Inefficiency — Multiple `br label add` calls\n1113\t\n1114\t**br (unbatched)**:\n1115\t```rust\n1116\tfor label in &labels {\n1117\t    br_label_add(id, label).await?;   // separate process per label\n1118\t}\n1119\t```\n1120\tN labels = N process invocations = N SQLite open/close cycles.\n1121\t\n1122\t**bf (batched)**:\n1123\t```bash\n1124\tbf label <id> add label1 label2 label3   # one INSERT per label, one transaction\n1125\t```\n1126\t\n1127\t### 5.6 Pluck Strand Update\n1128\t\n1129\tOne-line change in NEEDLE's `pluck.sh` or `bead_store/mod.rs`:\n1130\t\n1131\t```bash\n1132\t# Old (racy — two br calls with a race window between them):\n1133\t# br ready --json | pick_top | xargs br update --status in_progress --assignee \"$WORKER\"\n1134\t\n1135\t# New (atomic — single bf call, BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim):\n1136\tbead=$(bf claim --workspace \"$WORKSPACE\" --assignee \"$WORKER\" --json)\n1137\t```\n1138\t\n1139\t### 5.7 Close/Block Remains Same\n1140\t\n1141\t```bash\n1142\tbf close \"$bead_id\" --reason \"Completed: ...\"\n1143\tbf update \"$bead_id\" --status blocked\n1144\t```\n1145\t\n1146\tThese are single-operation writes with no race condition — no change needed.\n1147\t\n1148\t### 5.8 Symlink for Backward Compatibility\n1149\t\n1150\t```bash\n1151\tln -sf ~/.local/bin/bf ~/.local/bin/br\n1152\t```\n1153\t\n1154\tAll existing scripts using `br` commands work without modification. NEEDLE's non-atomic chains are replaced incrementally — `bf claim` and `bf batch` are the high-priority fixes; the rest can migrate when convenient.\n1155\t\n1156\t---\n1157\t\n1158\t## Phase 6: Build & Deploy\n1159\t\n1160\t### 6.1 Project Structure\n1161\t\n1162\t```\n1163\tbead-forge/\n1164\t├── Cargo.toml\n1165\t├── src/\n1166\t│   ├── main.rs              # No daemon, no systemd unit — each `bf` invocation is self-contained.\n1250\t\n1251\t---\n1252\t\n1253\t## Phase 7: Upstream Robustness Parity (br backports)\n1254\t\n1255\tUpstream `beads_rust` has kept shipping at remarkable velocity since the fork (reference:\n1256\t`Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust` `main` @ `8bff67a`, 2026-07-21 — nearly 400 issues worked,\n1257\tmost of them hardening the exact dual-store failure modes bf has hit in production). This\n1258\tphase ports the **robustness behaviors** into bf's architecture. Concepts only, not code —\n1259\tthe codebases have diverged too far to merge, upstream accepts no PRs (one-way flow), and\n1260\tattribution is carried here (beads_rust is MIT). Product-surface breadth is explicitly out\n1261\tof scope (see Non-goals).\n1262\t\n1263\tItems are ordered P0 → P2. Each maps to a standing bf pain point documented in incident\n1264\tmemory or CLAUDE.md.\n1265\t\n1266\t### 7.1 Incremental auto-flush + dirty tracking (P0) — amends Core Principle 2\n1267\t\n1268\tThe single highest-value port. Upstream writes the JSONL after every successful mutation;\n1269\tbf's flush-on-demand model is why db-only beads exist and why CLAUDE.md carries the\n1270\t\"ALWAYS `bf sync --flush-only` before repair\" ritual (post-2026-06-10 wipe).\n1271\t\n1272\t- New `dirty_issues` table (`issue_id`, `marked_at`); every mutation marks its issue dirty.\n1273\t- After each successful mutation: best-effort incremental export of *dirty rows only* into\n1274\t  the JSONL (surgical line replacement, not full rewrite). On failure: warn loudly (stderr\n1275\t  + `warning` field in the `--json` envelope), keep the dirty marks, never fail the\n1276\t  mutation. Named recovery: `bf sync --flush-only`.\n1277\t- Config `sync.auto_flush` (default **true**); `--no-auto-flush` per-invocation override.\n1278\t- `bf batch` flushes once at transaction end, not per-op (write amplification).\n1279\t- Read-only and diagnostic commands never write the JSONL (upstream's #326 lesson:\n1280\t  status/doctor commands that rewrite the artifact create git churn and mask real drift).\n1281\t\n1282\t**Exit criteria:** the flush-before-repair ritual is deletable from CLAUDE.md; killing a\n1283\tworker at any point between mutation and flush loses nothing that `git diff .beads/` can't\n1284\tshow; flush failure is visible in machine-readable output.\n1285\t\n1286\t### 7.2 Doctor safety stack (P0)\n1287\t\n1288\tbf's current guard (refuse/flush-first before repair) is one check. Upstream's is a layered\n1289\tarchitecture; port the layers:\n1290\t\n1291\t1. **Healthy early-return** — `bf doctor --repair` on a workspace with no errors runs only\n1292\t   trivial fixers and exits; it must be provably impossible to reach the JSONL rebuild from\n1293\t   a healthy state.\n1294\t2. **Local repair first** — integrity-check triage, VACUUM/REINDEX, cache rebuilds. The\n1295\t   JSONL rebuild is the last resort, not the first tool.\n1296\t3. **Verified pre-rebuild backups** — SHA-256-hashed copies of the full DB family into a\n1297\t   recovery dir before any rebuild; restore-on-failure; `bf doctor runs` / `bf doctor\n1298\t   restore <run-id|latest>` to list and roll back.\n1299\t4. **JSONL authority preflight** — refuse rebuild if the JSONL contains merge-conflict\n1300\t   markers or invalid records (rebuilding from a poisoned authority is how a bad flush\n1301\t   becomes permanent).\n1302\t5. **Repeat-failure refusal** — a rebuild whose post-verification failed writes a marker;\n1303\t   further rebuilds refuse without `--allow-repeated-repair`.\n1304\t6. **Preservation across rebuild** — snapshot unflushed **dirty issues** (with labels,\n1305\t   dependencies, comments) *and* tombstones before rebuild; restore and re-mark dirty\n1306\t   after; report the count in the repair summary. This is `beads_rust#394` (filed by us\n1307\t   upstream 2026-07-21) — implement it here first.\n1308\t\n1309\t**Exit criteria:** an induced rebuild on a workspace with unflushed beads loses nothing;\n1310\trepair on a healthy workspace is a no-op; every rebuild leaves a restorable, hash-verified\n1311\tbackup.\n1312\t\n1313\t### 7.3 NULL-datetime & schema hardening (P0, small)\n1314\t\n1315\tFix the `parse_datetime` crash on NULL datetime columns (the flush/list crash class that\n1316\tpreviously forced the destructive `rm beads.db + reimport` workaround). Add a doctor\n1317\tdetector + repair fixer for NULL-in-NOT-NULL rows generally.\n1318\t\n1319\t### 7.4 Anomaly classification & sync verdicts (P1)\n1320\t\n1321\t- An `AnomalyClass` enum with severity tiers: `DbNewer`, `JsonlNewer`, `CountMismatch`,\n1322\t  `IdSetMismatch`, `ConflictMarkers`, `DatabaseCorrupt`, … surfaced uniformly in\n1323\t  `bf doctor --json`.\n1324\t- `bf sync --status` renders an **\"In sync\" verdict** backed by evidence: stored\n1325\t  `jsonl_content_hash` matches computed hash AND `dirty_issues` is empty.\n1326\t\n1327\t**Exit criteria:** the manual corruption-triage ritual (compare `git log -1 issues.jsonl`\n1328\tagainst bead counts) is replaced by one command with a machine-readable verdict.\n1329\t\n1330\t### 7.5 `update` description editing (P1)\n1331\t\n1332\t`bf update --description` / `--description-file` / `--acceptance-criteria` — closes the\n1333\tdocumented \"bf update cannot edit description; add a comment instead\" gap. Lesson from\n1334\tupstream's #386 regression: the fix must be wired through the real update path and covered\n1335\tby a round-trip integration test (their first fix for this shipped without ever touching\n1336\t`update.rs`).\n1337\t\n1338\t### 7.6 Batch surface expansion (P1)\n1339\t\n1340\t`bf batch` today supports only create/dep_add_blocker/close. Expand to a uniform op set\n1341\t(update, label add/remove, dep add/remove, comment) inside one transaction with one\n1342\tauto-flush at the end. The bf-5id blocked→open cascade must hold identically in the batch\n1343\tclose path.\n1344\t\n1345\t### 7.7 JSON contract discipline (P1)\n1346\t\n1347\t- One stable envelope shape for every command's `--json` output — fixes the\n1348\t  `bf ready` (JSON array) vs `bf list` (NDJSON) divergence that silently miscounts under\n1349\t  `json.load`.\n1350\t- `bf robot-docs`: machine-readable enumeration of every command's contract, for agent\n1351\t  consumers (NEEDLE worker prompts reference it instead of hardcoding shapes).\n1352\t\n1353\t### 7.8 Derived blocked status (P2 — architectural)\n1354\t\n1355\tUpstream computes blocked-ness from the dependency graph (with a `blocked_issues_cache`\n1356\tinvalidated on dep/close mutations) instead of storing a status that must be transitioned.\n1357\tThis deletes the bf-5id bug class (stuck-blocked beads stalling workers) at the root — the\n1358\tjust-shipped cascade fix treats the symptom.\n1359\t\n1360\t**Hard constraint:** NEEDLE's safe-dispatch fences beads by manually setting\n1361\t`status=blocked`. A derived model MUST retain an explicit manual hold that presents as\n1362\tblocked and takes precedence over the derived value (dedicated flag or a preserved manual\n1363\tstatus — decide at design time, with NEEDLE-side review). CLI and JSONL compatibility:\n1364\tconsumers keep seeing `status: \"blocked\"`.\n1365\t\n1366\tIncludes a migration for existing stored-blocked rows.\n1367\t\n1368\t### 7.9 Multi-box & fleet concurrency (P2)\n1369\t\n1370\t- **Merge anchor** (`beads.base.jsonl`): a base snapshot enabling 3-way merge of JSONL\n1371\t  across checkouts — targets the recurring lab/ex44 divergence.\n1372\t- **Concurrent-writer hardening**: fleet-scale tests (N concurrent `bf` processes doing\n1373\t  create/claim/close) hunting the upstream-documented classes — parallel-write silent loss,\n1374\t  spurious sync conflicts during auto-import.\n1375\t- **Pre-export history backups** (`.bf_history/` with prune policy): one more insurance\n1376\t  layer under the JSONL, cheap to keep.\n1377\t\n1378\t### Non-goals\n1379\t\n1380\tUpstream surface deliberately NOT ported: the MCP server, workflow gates /\n1381\ttransition-scoped required fields, scheduler, agent-coordination module, epic containment,\n1382\tcapacity/admission control, and graph-analytics TUI. NEEDLE owns orchestration in this\n1383\tstack; `bv` exists for visualization; bf's identity is the lean, fleet-hardened store.\n1384\tPreserve bf's own differentiators upstream lacks: atomic `claim`, `critical_path`,\n1385\t`velocity`, `commit_check`, secret scanning, genesis beads, annotations.\n1386\t\n1387\t### Open questions\n1388\t\n1389\t- Auto-flush × rotation: incremental flush must target only the active `issues.jsonl`,\n1390\t  never archives — confirm rotation interplay before 7.1 ships.\n1391\t- Does auto-flush change git-commit cadence guidance for NEEDLE workers (`.beads/` will now\n1392\t  be dirty far more often between commits)?\n1393\t- 7.8 manual-hold representation (new flag vs preserved manual status) needs NEEDLE-side\n1394\t  review before implementation — do not start 7.8 until that decision is recorded here.\n1395\t\n1396\t---\n1397\t\n1398\t## Test Strategy & Isolation\n1399\t\n1400\tbf must be testable without touching, modifying, or interfering with any live `br` workspace. Three isolation concerns drive the test strategy:\n1401\t\n1402\t### Rule 1: Never Share a Live Database\n1403\t\n1404\tbf tests **never** auto-discover or open a `.beads/beads.db` that `br` is actively using. SQLite WAL mode serializes writers, so concurrent opens are safe from a corruption standpoint — but test mutations (creates, claims, closes) would contaminate real workspaces with spurious beads.\n1405\t\n1406\tAll tests target exactly one of:\n1407\t- **`:memory:`** — rusqlite in-memory database (unit tests, zero disk I/O)\n1408\t- **`tempfile::tempdir()`** — ephemeral directory deleted on drop (integration tests)\n1409\t- **Read-only fixture copy** — `issues.jsonl` copied out of a real workspace into a tempdir, never written back (compat tests)\n1410\t\n1411\t### Rule 2: Never Point `br` at a bf Test Database\n1412\t\n1413\tThe schema compat test must verify `br` can read a `bf`-created database — but it cannot use br's own workspace for this. The test creates a fresh tempdir, runs `bf init` + `bf create` in it, then invokes `br --db /path/to/temp/beads.db` against that file. The real `br` workspace is untouched.\n1414\t\n1415\t### Rule 3: JSONL Fixture = Read-Only Copy\n1416\t\n1417\tThe JSONL round-trip test uses a snapshot of a real workspace's `issues.jsonl` as a fixture, not a live file. The fixture is checked into `tests/fixtures/` (or copied at test time with `--allow-stale`). `bf sync --import` loads it into a tempdir database; `bf list --format json` is compared against the expected output derived from `br list --format json` run against the same snapshot.\n1418\t\n1419\t```\n1420\ttests/fixtures/\n1421\t├── forge-snapshot.jsonl    # snapshot of FORGE workspace (committed, static)\n1422\t└── needle-snapshot.jsonl   # snapshot of NEEDLE workspace\n1423\t```\n1424\t\n1425\tThese fixtures are updated manually when the schema changes: `cp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl tests/fixtures/forge-snapshot.jsonl`.\n1426\t\n1427\t### Test Harness (`tests/common/mod.rs`)\n1428\t\n1429\t```rust\n1430\tpub struct TempWorkspace {\n1431\t    dir: tempfile::TempDir,   // deleted on drop — no cleanup needed\n1432\t    pub db_path: PathBuf,\n1433\t    pub storage: Storage,\n1434\t}\n1435\t\n1436\timpl TempWorkspace {\n1437\t    pub fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n1438\t        let dir = tempfile::tempdir()?;\n1439\t        let db_path = dir.path().join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n1440\t        fs::create_dir(dir.path().join(\".beads\"))?;\n1441\t        let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n1442\t        Ok(Self { dir, db_path, storage })\n1443\t    }\n1444\t\n1445\t    pub fn from_fixture(jsonl: &Path) -> Result<Self> {\n1446\t        let ws = Self::new()?;\n1447\t        import_jsonl(jsonl, &ws.storage)?;\n1448\t        Ok(ws)\n1449\t    }\n1450\t\n1451\t    // Run br against this workspace's db (for compat tests)\n1452\t    pub fn br(&self, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {\n1453\t        Command::new(\"br\")\n1454\t            .arg(\"--db\").arg(&self.db_path)\n1455\t            .args(args)\n1456\t            .output()\n1457\t            .expect(\"br not in PATH\")\n1458\t    }\n1459\t}\n1460\t```\n1461\t\n1462\tUnit tests in `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `Storage::open(\":memory:\")` directly — no `TempWorkspace` needed.\n1463\t\n1464\t### Schema Forward-Compatibility\n1465\t\n1466\tbf adds tables that br doesn't know about. No columns are added to the shared `issues` table.\n1467\t\n1468\t| Addition | br behavior |\n1469\t|----------|-------------|\n1470\t| `bead_annotations` table | br ignores unknown tables entirely; `issues` column count is unchanged so `issues_column_order_matches()` passes and `rebuild_issues_table()` never fires |\n1471\t| `worker_sessions` table | Same — ignored |\n1472\t| `velocity_stats` table | Same — ignored |\n1473\t| `critical_path_cache` table | Same — ignored |\n1474\t\n1475\t**Why no column on `issues`**: br's `issues_column_order_matches()` in `schema.rs:630` checks `actual_columns.len() != EXPECTED_ISSUE_COLUMN_ORDER.len()`. Any extra column causes this to return `false`, which triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` — a full DROP + recreate using only br's canonical column list. An `annotations` column on `issues` would be silently destroyed on every `br` open. Storing annotations in `bead_annotations` sidesteps this entirely.\n1476\t\n1477\tMigration on `Storage::open` (fully idempotent — all `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`):\n1478\t\n1479\t```rust\n1480\tfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> Result<()> {\n1481\t    conn.execute_batch(\"\n1482\t        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bead_annotations (\n1483\t            bead_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n1484\t            key     TEXT NOT NULL,\n1485\t            value   TEXT NOT NULL,\n1486\t            PRIMARY KEY (bead_id, key)\n1487\t        );\n1488\t        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bead_annotations_key_value\n1489\t            ON bead_annotations (key, value);\n1490\t        -- other bf-only tables follow\n1491\t    \")?;\n1492\t    Ok(())\n1493\t}\n1494\t```\n1495\t\n1496\tNo `ALTER TABLE` on `issues`, ever. The migration is a pure table-creation pass.\n1497\t\n1498\t---\n1499\t\n1500\t## Compatibility Verification\n1501\t\n1502\tAll tests run against **isolated temp workspaces** — no live br workspace is touched.\n1503\t\n1504\t### JSONL Round-Trip Test\n1505\t\n1506\t```bash\n1507\t# 1. Copy real workspace JSONL as a read-only fixture (never modify the original)\n1508\tFIXTURE=$(mktemp -d)\n1509\tcp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n1510\t\n1511\t# 2. bf imports the fixture into a fresh tempdir\n1512\tBFDIR=$(mktemp -d)\n1513\tbf init --prefix fg --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1514\tbf sync --import-only --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" --jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n1515\t\n1516\t# 3. bf exports its view of the data\n1517\tbf list --format json --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" | jq -S '.' > /tmp/bf-output.jsonl\n1518\t\n1519\t# 4. br reads the original JSONL directly (read-only, not our tempdir)\n1520\tbr list --format json --db \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\" --no-db | jq -S '.' > /tmp/br-output.jsonl\n1521\t\n1522\t# 5.
