No daemon, no systemd unit — each `bf` invocation is self-contained.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 7: Upstream Robustness Parity (br backports)\n\nUpstream `beads_rust` has kept shipping at remarkable velocity since the fork (reference:\n`Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust` `main` @ `8bff67a`, 2026-07-21 — nearly 400 issues worked,\nmost of them hardening the exact dual-store failure modes bf has hit in production). This\nphase ports the **robustness behaviors** into bf's architecture. Concepts only, not code —\nthe codebases have diverged too far to merge, upstream accepts no PRs (one-way flow), and\nattribution is carried here (beads_rust is MIT). Product-surface breadth is explicitly out\nof scope (see Non-goals).\n\nItems are ordered P0 → P2. Each maps to a standing bf pain point documented in incident\nmemory or CLAUDE.md.\n\n### 7.1 Incremental auto-flush + dirty tracking (P0) — amends Core Principle 2\n\nThe single highest-value port. Upstream writes the JSONL after every successful mutation;\nbf's flush-on-demand model is why db-only beads exist and why CLAUDE.md carries the\n\"ALWAYS `bf sync --flush-only` before repair\" ritual (post-2026-06-10 wipe).\n\n- New `dirty_issues` table (`issue_id`, `marked_at`); every mutation marks its issue dirty.\n- After each successful mutation: best-effort incremental export of *dirty rows only* into\n  the JSONL (surgical line replacement, not full rewrite). On failure: warn loudly (stderr\n  + `warning` field in the `--json` envelope), keep the dirty marks, never fail the\n  mutation. Named recovery: `bf sync --flush-only`.\n- Config `sync.auto_flush` (default **true**); `--no-auto-flush` per-invocation override.\n- `bf batch` flushes once at transaction end, not per-op (write amplification).\n- Read-only and diagnostic commands never write the JSONL (upstream's #326 lesson:\n  status/doctor commands that rewrite the artifact create git churn and mask real drift).\n\n**Exit criteria:** the flush-before-repair ritual is deletable from CLAUDE.md; killing a\nworker at any point between mutation and flush loses nothing that `git diff .beads/` can't\nshow; flush failure is visible in machine-readable output.\n\n### 7.2 Doctor safety stack (P0)\n\nbf's current guard (refuse/flush-first before repair) is one check. Upstream's is a layered\narchitecture; port the layers:\n\n1. **Healthy early-return** — `bf doctor --repair` on a workspace with no errors runs only\n   trivial fixers and exits; it must be provably impossible to reach the JSONL rebuild from\n   a healthy state.\n2. **Local repair first** — integrity-check triage, VACUUM/REINDEX, cache rebuilds. The\n   JSONL rebuild is the last resort, not the first tool.\n3. **Verified pre-rebuild backups** — SHA-256-hashed copies of the full DB family into a\n   recovery dir before any rebuild; restore-on-failure; `bf doctor runs` / `bf doctor\n   restore <run-id|latest>` to list and roll back.\n4. **JSONL authority preflight** — refuse rebuild if the JSONL contains merge-conflict\n   markers or invalid records (rebuilding from a poisoned authority is how a bad flush\n   becomes permanent).\n5. **Repeat-failure refusal** — a rebuild whose post-verification failed writes a marker;\n   further rebuilds refuse without `--allow-repeated-repair`.\n6. **Preservation across rebuild** — snapshot unflushed **dirty issues** (with labels,\n   dependencies, comments) *and* tombstones before rebuild; restore and re-mark dirty\n   after; report the count in the repair summary. This is `beads_rust#394` (filed by us\n   upstream 2026-07-21) — implement it here first.\n\n**Exit criteria:** an induced rebuild on a workspace with unflushed beads loses nothing;\nrepair on a healthy workspace is a no-op; every rebuild leaves a restorable, hash-verified\nbackup.\n\n### 7.3 NULL-datetime & schema hardening (P0, small)\n\nFix the `parse_datetime` crash on NULL datetime columns (the flush/list crash class that\npreviously forced the destructive `rm beads.db + reimport` workaround). Add a doctor\ndetector + repair fixer for NULL-in-NOT-NULL rows generally.\n\n### 7.4 Anomaly classification & sync verdicts (P1)\n\n- An `AnomalyClass` enum with severity tiers: `DbNewer`, `JsonlNewer`, `CountMismatch`,\n  `IdSetMismatch`, `ConflictMarkers`, `DatabaseCorrupt`, … surfaced uniformly in\n  `bf doctor --json`.\n- `bf sync --status` renders an **\"In sync\" verdict** backed by evidence: stored\n  `jsonl_content_hash` matches computed hash AND `dirty_issues` is empty.\n\n**Exit criteria:** the manual corruption-triage ritual (compare `git log -1 issues.jsonl`\nagainst bead counts) is replaced by one command with a machine-readable verdict.\n\n### 7.5 `update` description editing (P1)\n\n`bf update --description` / `--description-file` / `--acceptance-criteria` — closes the\ndocumented \"bf update cannot edit description; add a comment instead\" gap. Lesson from\nupstream's #386 regression: the fix must be wired through the real update path and covered\nby a round-trip integration test (their first fix for this shipped without ever touching\n`update.rs`).\n\n### 7.6 Batch surface expansion (P1)\n\n`bf batch` today supports only create/dep_add_blocker/close. Expand to a uniform op set\n(update, label add/remove, dep add/remove, comment) inside one transaction with one\nauto-flush at the end. The bf-5id blocked→open cascade must hold identically in the batch\nclose path.\n\n### 7.7 JSON contract discipline (P1)\n\n- One stable envelope shape for every command's `--json` output — fixes the\n  `bf ready` (JSON array) vs `bf list` (NDJSON) divergence that silently miscounts under\n  `json.load`.\n- `bf robot-docs`: machine-readable enumeration of every command's contract, for agent\n  consumers (NEEDLE worker prompts reference it instead of hardcoding shapes).\n\n### 7.8 Derived blocked status (P2 — architectural)\n\nUpstream computes blocked-ness from the dependency graph (with a `blocked_issues_cache`\ninvalidated on dep/close mutations) instead of storing a status that must be transitioned.\nThis deletes the bf-5id bug class (stuck-blocked beads stalling workers) at the root — the\njust-shipped cascade fix treats the symptom.\n\n**Hard constraint:** NEEDLE's safe-dispatch fences beads by manually setting\n`status=blocked`. A derived model MUST retain an explicit manual hold that presents as\nblocked and takes precedence over the derived value (dedicated flag or a preserved manual\nstatus — decide at design time, with NEEDLE-side review). CLI and JSONL compatibility:\nconsumers keep seeing `status: \"blocked\"`.\n\nIncludes a migration for existing stored-blocked rows.\n\n### 7.9 Multi-box & fleet concurrency (P2)\n\n- **Merge anchor** (`beads.base.jsonl`): a base snapshot enabling 3-way merge of JSONL\n  across checkouts — targets the recurring lab/ex44 divergence.\n- **Concurrent-writer hardening**: fleet-scale tests (N concurrent `bf` processes doing\n  create/claim/close) hunting the upstream-documented classes — parallel-write silent loss,\n  spurious sync conflicts during auto-import.\n- **Pre-export history backups** (`.bf_history/` with prune policy): one more insurance\n  layer under the JSONL, cheap to keep.\n\n### Non-goals\n\nUpstream surface deliberately NOT ported: the MCP server, workflow gates /\ntransition-scoped required fields, scheduler, agent-coordination module, epic containment,\ncapacity/admission control, and graph-analytics TUI. NEEDLE owns orchestration in this\nstack; `bv` exists for visualization; bf's identity is the lean, fleet-hardened store.\nPreserve bf's own differentiators upstream lacks: atomic `claim`, `critical_path`,\n`velocity`, `commit_check`, secret scanning, genesis beads, annotations.\n\n### Open questions\n\n- Auto-flush × rotation: incremental flush must target only the active `issues.jsonl`,\n  never archives — confirm rotation interplay before 7.1 ships.\n- Does auto-flush change git-commit cadence guidance for NEEDLE workers (`.beads/` will now\n  be dirty far more often between commits)?\n- 7.8 manual-hold representation (new flag vs preserved manual status) needs NEEDLE-side\n  review before implementation — do not start 7.8 until that decision is recorded here.\n\n---\n\n## Test Strategy & Isolation\n\nbf must be testable without touching, modifying, or interfering with any live `br` workspace. Three isolation concerns drive the test strategy:\n\n### Rule 1: Never Share a Live Database\n\nbf tests **never** auto-discover or open a `.beads/beads.db` that `br` is actively using. SQLite WAL mode serializes writers, so concurrent opens are safe from a corruption standpoint — but test mutations (creates, claims, closes) would contaminate real workspaces with spurious beads.\n\nAll tests target exactly one of:\n- **`:memory:`** — rusqlite in-memory database (unit tests, zero disk I/O)\n- **`tempfile::tempdir()`** — ephemeral directory deleted on drop (integration tests)\n- **Read-only fixture copy** — `issues.jsonl` copied out of a real workspace into a tempdir, never written back (compat tests)\n\n### Rule 2: Never Point `br` at a bf Test Database\n\nThe schema compat test must verify `br` can read a `bf`-created database — but it cannot use br's own workspace for this. The test creates a fresh tempdir, runs `bf init` + `bf create` in it, then invokes `br --db /path/to/temp/beads.db` against that file. The real `br` workspace is untouched.\n\n### Rule 3: JSONL Fixture = Read-Only Copy\n\nThe JSONL round-trip test uses a snapshot of a real workspace's `issues.jsonl` as a fixture, not a live file. The fixture is checked into `tests/fixtures/` (or copied at test time with `--allow-stale`). `bf sync --import` loads it into a tempdir database; `bf list --format json` is compared against the expected output derived from `br list --format json` run against the same snapshot.\n\n```\ntests/fixtures/\n├── forge-snapshot.jsonl    # snapshot of FORGE workspace (committed, static)\n└── needle-snapshot.jsonl   # snapshot of NEEDLE workspace\n```\n\nThese fixtures are updated manually when the schema changes: `cp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl tests/fixtures/forge-snapshot.jsonl`.\n\n### Test Harness (`tests/common/mod.rs`)\n\n```rust\npub struct TempWorkspace {\n    dir: tempfile::TempDir,   // deleted on drop — no cleanup needed\n    pub db_path: PathBuf,\n    pub storage: Storage,\n}\n\nimpl TempWorkspace {\n    pub fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n        let dir = tempfile::tempdir()?;\n        let db_path = dir.path().join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n        fs::create_dir(dir.path().join(\".beads\"))?;\n        let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n        Ok(Self { dir, db_path, storage })\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_fixture(jsonl: &Path) -> Result<Self> {\n        let ws = Self::new()?;\n        import_jsonl(jsonl, &ws.storage)?;\n        Ok(ws)\n    }\n\n    // Run br against this workspace's db (for compat tests)\n    pub fn br(&self, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {\n        Command::new(\"br\")\n            .arg(\"--db\").arg(&self.db_path)\n            .args(args)\n            .output()\n            .expect(\"br not in PATH\")\n    }\n}\n```\n\nUnit tests in `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `Storage::open(\":memory:\")` directly — no `TempWorkspace` needed.\n\n### Schema Forward-Compatibility\n\nbf adds tables that br doesn't know about. No columns are added to the shared `issues` table.\n\n| Addition | br behavior |\n|----------|-------------|\n| `bead_annotations` table | br ignores unknown tables entirely; `issues` column count is unchanged so `issues_column_order_matches()` passes and `rebuild_issues_table()` never fires |\n| `worker_sessions` table | Same — ignored |\n| `velocity_stats` table | Same — ignored |\n| `critical_path_cache` table | Same — ignored |\n\n**Why no column on `issues`**: br's `issues_column_order_matches()` in `schema.rs:630` checks `actual_columns.len() != EXPECTED_ISSUE_COLUMN_ORDER.len()`. Any extra column causes this to return `false`, which triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` — a full DROP + recreate using only br's canonical column list. An `annotations` column on `issues` would be silently destroyed on every `br` open. Storing annotations in `bead_annotations` sidesteps this entirely.\n\nMigration on `Storage::open` (fully idempotent — all `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`):\n\n```rust\nfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> Result<()> {\n    conn.execute_batch(\"\n        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bead_annotations (\n            bead_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n            key     TEXT NOT NULL,\n            value   TEXT NOT NULL,\n            PRIMARY KEY (bead_id, key)\n        );\n        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bead_annotations_key_value\n            ON bead_annotations (key, value);\n        -- other bf-only tables follow\n    \")?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n```\n\nNo `ALTER TABLE` on `issues`, ever. The migration is a pure table-creation pass.\n\n---\n\n## Compatibility Verification\n\nAll tests run against **isolated temp workspaces** — no live br workspace is touched.\n\n### JSONL Round-Trip Test\n\n```bash\n# 1. Copy real workspace JSONL as a read-only fixture (never modify the original)\nFIXTURE=$(mktemp -d)\ncp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n\n# 2. bf imports the fixture into a fresh tempdir\nBFDIR=$(mktemp -d)\nbf init --prefix fg --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\nbf sync --import-only --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" --jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n\n# 3. bf exports its view of the data\nbf list --format json --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" | jq -S '.' > /tmp/bf-output.jsonl\n\n# 4. br reads the original JSONL directly (read-only, not our tempdir)\nbr list --format json --db \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\" --no-db | jq -S '.' > /tmp/br-output.jsonl\n\n# 5. Compare (order-independent by ID)\ndiff /tmp/bf-output.jsonl /tmp/br-output.jsonl\n# Must be empty — bf and br produce identical output from the same JSONL\n\n# Cleanup\nrm -rf \"$FIXTURE\" \"$BFDIR\"\n```\n\n### Schema Forward-Compatibility Test\n\n```bash\n# 1. bf creates a workspace in a fresh tempdir (bf schema, including bf-only tables)\nBFDIR=$(mktemp -d)\nbf init --prefix fg --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\nbf create --title \"compat test\" --type task --priority 1 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\nbf create --title \"another bead\" --type bug --priority 0 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\nbf annotate fg-xxx needle_attempt=1 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n# Annotation is stored in bead_annotations table, NOT in issues column\n\n# 2. br opens the same file (not its own workspace — pointed explicitly at the temp db)\nbr list --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"         # must list 2 beads without error\nbr doctor --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"       # must pass integrity check\n# Key assertion: br's issues_column_order_matches() sees exact column count → passes\n# rebuild_issues_table() is NOT triggered → bead_annotations table untouched\nbr update fg-xxx --status closed --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"  # must succeed\n\n# 3. bf re-reads the br-mutated database (bead_annotations must survive br's UPDATE)\nbf show fg-xxx --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" --json | jq '.annotations'\n# Must still contain {\"needle_attempt\": \"1\"} — annotation row in bead_annotations\n# is untouched by br's UPDATE to the issues table\n\n# Cleanup\nrm -rf \"$BFDIR\"\n```\n\n### Reverse Compatibility Test\n\n```bash\n# 1. br creates a workspace (br schema — no bead_annotations table, no velocity_stats table)\nBRDIR=$(mktemp -d)\nbr init --prefix fg --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"\nbr create \"br-created bead\" --type task --priority 2 --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"\n\n# 2. bf opens the br-created database\n# Storage::open runs apply_migrations() which creates bead_annotations + other bf-only\n# tables via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. No ALTER TABLE on issues is needed.\nbf list --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"         # must list the br-created bead without error\nbf annotate fg-yyy test_key=hello --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"  # inserts into bead_annotations\nbf show fg-yyy --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\" --json | jq '.annotations'\n# Must contain {\"test_key\": \"hello\"} — fetched via JOIN on bead_annotations\n\n# 3. br can still read the migrated database (new tables are ignored by br)\n# Critical: issues table column count is still exactly what br expects\nbr list --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"         # must still work\nbr doctor --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"       # must still pass — no issues column changes\n\n# Cleanup\nrm -rf \"$BRDIR\"\n```\n\n### Claim Race Test\n\n```bash\n# Setup: create a test workspace with 10 beads of varying priority\ncd /tmp && rm -rf bf-test && mkdir bf-test && cd bf-test && bf init --prefix bf\nfor i in $(seq 1 10); do\n  bf create --title \"test-$i\" --priority $((i % 5))\ndone\n\n# === Test 1: Basic thundering herd (20 workers, 10 beads) ===\n# 20 workers claim simultaneously. Exactly 10 get a bead, 10 get NONE.\nfor i in $(seq 1 20); do\n  bf claim --any --assignee \"worker-$i\" --json > /tmp/claim-$i.out 2>&1 &\ndone\nwait\n\n# Verify: exactly 10 claims succeeded, 10 returned NONE\ngrep -cl '\"id\"' /tmp/claim-*.out | wc -l  # must be 10\ngrep -cl 'NONE' /tmp/claim-*.out | wc -l  # must be 10\n\n# Verify: no bead claimed by more than one worker\ncat /tmp/claim-*.out | jq -r '.id' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn\n# Every ID must appear exactly once\n\n# === Test 2: Priority ordering ===\n# The 10 workers that succeeded should have beads in priority order\n# (priority 0 beads claimed before priority 4)\n# Verify by correlating claim output order with priority values\n\n# === Test 3: Sequential claims (depletion) ===\n# Create 20 more beads, claim one at a time, verify queue drains\nfor i in $(seq 11 30); do\n  bf create --title \"test-$i\" --priority $((i % 5))\ndone\nfor i in $(seq 1 20); do\n  result=$(bf claim --any --assignee \"seq-worker-$i\" --json)\n  [ -n \"$result\" ] && echo \"$result\" | jq -r '.id'\ndone\nbf list --status open --format json\n# Must return empty — all beads claimed\n\n# === Test 4: Stale claim reclamation ===\n# Claim a bead, manually age its updated_at past claim_ttl\n# Then claim again — the stale bead should be reclaimed and re-claimable\nbf claim --any --assignee \"dead-worker\" --json\n# (test harness: set claim_ttl to 5s for this test, or mock updated_at)\nbf doctor --reclaim-stale --ttl 0s\nbf list --status open --format json\n# The dead-worker's bead must be back in open status\n\n# === Test 5: Stale reclamation as side effect ===\n# Dead worker's bead is reclaimed when another worker claims\nbf claim --any --assignee \"scavenger\" --json\n# scavenger gets a bead; dead-worker's bead is also reclaimed to open\n\n# === Test 6: Multi-workspace claiming ===\n# Create two workspaces, claim --any gets highest priority across both\nmkdir /tmp/ws-a && cd /tmp/ws-a && bf init --prefix wa\nmkdir /tmp/ws-b && cd /tmp/ws-b && bf init --prefix wb\nbf create --title \"ws-a high\" --priority 0   # in ws-b\nbf create --title \"ws-a low\"  --priority 4   # in ws-b\ncd /tmp/ws-a && bf create --title \"ws-a mid\" --priority 2\nbf claim --any --assignee \"multi-worker\" --json --workspace /tmp/ws-a --workspace /tmp/ws-b\n# Should get ws-b's \"ws-a high\" (priority 0)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Order\n\n| Phase | Description | Estimated Effort |\n|-------|-------------|-----------------|\n| 1 | Core library (model, JSONL read/write, config, ID gen) | Foundation |\n| 2 | SQLite cache layer (schema, storage, sync, doctor) | Medium |\n| 3 | CLI commands (all br-compatible commands) | Medium |\n| 4 | Concurrent claiming (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, impact scoring, stale reclamation, multi-workspace) | Medium |\n| 4B | Extended features (log rotation, batch ops, annotations, operation history, secret scanning, critical path, velocity scoring) | Medium |\n| 5 | NEEDLE integration (pluck.sh update, backward compat) | Small |\n| 6 | Build & deploy (CI, binary) | Small |\n| 7 | Upstream robustness parity: auto-flush + dirty tracking, doctor safety stack, NULL hardening, anomaly verdicts, update/batch/JSON-contract gaps, derived blocked, multi-box concurrency | Medium-Large |\n\nPhases 1-3 produce a fully functional standalone `bf` that replaces `br`. Phase 4 adds atomic claiming for fleet operations. Phase 4B adds extended features that make bf more powerful than br. Phases 5-6 integrate and deploy. Phase 7 (added 2026-07-21) back-ports the robustness behaviors upstream `beads_rust` developed after the fork — P0 items first (7.1-7.3), then P1 (7.4-7.7), then the architectural/multi-box P2 items (7.8-7.9).\n\n---\n\n## Key Design Decisions\n\n1. **SQLite-primary, JSONL as git artifact**: SQLite is the live database — all reads and writes go through it. JSONL is exported on `bf sync` for git commit, providing backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. This matches how bd and br work, but with rusqlite (no corruption) and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim (no race condition).\n\n2. **rusqlite, not FrankenSQLite**: We already proved in the beads_rust fork that FrankenSQLite has corruption issues. Start clean with rusqlite.\n\n3. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim**: The read-score-update sequence runs in a single SQLite write transaction. No flock, no streaming rewrite, no temp files. SQLite's own locking serializes concurrent claims correctly.\n\n4. **No automatic git commits**: Match br's explicit, non-invasive philosophy. Users run `bf sync` when they want to commit JSONL changes.\n\n5. **Cattle, not pets**: Workers are disposable fleet units with no identity, no memory, and no conversation. Claims are atomic SQL dequeues from a priority queue, not negotiations.\n\n6. **Stale reclamation as a side effect of claiming**: The first statement in every `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` claim transaction resets expired `in_progress` beads. No separate heartbeat system, no background process.\n\n7. **Server as future optimization, not v1**: A persistent in-memory server would reduce per-claim latency from ~2ms to ~0.1ms by eliminating SQLite file I/O. Premature for current scale — can be added transparently later.\n\n8. **Rotation keeps JSONL artifact lean**: Closed beads older than `rotate_age_days` are exported to archive files (`issues.jsonl.1`, etc.) rather than the active `issues.jsonl`. Keeps the committed artifact small and git diffs readable.\n\n9. **Annotations as extension mechanism**: Arbitrary `BTreeMap<String, String>` on beads lets external tools (NEEDLE, custom scripts) store structured metadata without schema changes. Stored in a separate `bead_annotations` table — never as a column on `issues` — because br's `issues_column_order_matches()` triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` on any column count mismatch, silently destroying any extra column on every br open. br never reads or writes `bead_annotations`, so annotation data survives any br operation unchanged.\n\n10. **Events table for history**: Every mutation records an event row. `bf log` queries the events table — O(1) by issue ID. Long-term history via git log on `issues.jsonl`.\n\n11. **Secret scanning before write**: Built-in regex-based secret detection prevents credentials from entering SQLite or the JSONL export. Configurable patterns, git pre-commit hook integration.\n\n12. **`.beads/` is committed to git**: `issues.jsonl` + config are version-controlled. `beads.db` is gitignored (binary, rebuilt from JSONL on `bf sync --import`). Secret scanning protects the exported JSONL.\n\n13. **Critical path drives claim priority, not just listed priority**: Listed priority is a human signal, but it decays as the project evolves and humans stop curating it. Critical path float is computed from the live dependency graph and is always current. A priority-3 bead on the critical path outranks a priority-0 bead with float=5 — the fleet naturally works on what matters most without human recuration.\n\n14. **Worker composition is first-class metadata**: `--model`, `--harness`, `--harness-version` on `bf claim` record what kind of agent did the work. This transforms the events table from a bare audit log into a performance dataset: which model+harness combinations close which task types fastest. The fleet becomes self-optimizing — velocity data informs which workers to dispatch to which workspace, without any external ML pipeline.\n\n15. **Upstream br is a tracked ideas source, ported one-way as behaviors, never merged as code** (2026-07-21): beads_rust keeps solving dual-store robustness problems bf also has — credit where due, Emanuel keeps finding improvements on top of what already exists. The codebases are architecturally divergent and upstream accepts no PRs (their agents integrate from filed issues), so the flow is: study upstream behavior → spec it against bf's architecture in this plan (Phase 7) → implement natively with attribution. Never vendor upstream code, never chase their product surface (see Phase 7 Non-goals), and periodically re-scan their tracker/source for new robustness work worth porting.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Decision Records\n\n### ADR-1: Periodic `.beads/` git checkpoint timer (2026-07-20)\n\n**Status:** Accepted & implemented — `bf-checkpoint.{sh,service,timer}` ship in `deploy/` (Debian/Ubuntu) and `systemd/` (NixOS); `CheckpointConfig` parses the block in `src/config.rs`. Parent bead: `bf-48pw0`.\n\n**Context.** bead-forge is a dual-store system: SQLite (`beads.db`) is the live store and `issues.jsonl` is the git-tracked checkpoint (see Core Principle #2 and §2.7). Historically, mutations did not auto-flush, so a workspace under active NEEDLE work could accumulate **db-only** beads never captured in git — losing the box meant losing work, and shared workspaces (many agents in one tree) had no coherent, low-noise way to land periodic snapshots. Phase 7.1's `sync.auto_flush` (default on) closes the per-mutation gap, but a periodic out-of-band safety net is still wanted so that even a workspace whose agents exit ungracefully still gets its state committed to git.\n\n**Decision.** A dedicated systemd timer (`bf-checkpoint.timer` → `bf-checkpoint.service` → `bf-checkpoint.sh`) periodically flushes SQLite → JSONL via `bf sync --flush-only` and, if `.beads/issues.jsonl` changed, stages **only** that file and commits it as `chore(beads): auto-checkpoint <UTC>`. It runs strictly out-of-band — driven by the timer, never by any `bf` command. New rollouts default to **`checkpoint.enabled: false`**; a maintainer must opt each workspace in. `git push` is off by default.\n\n**Consequences.**\n\n- **Out-of-band only.** `src/claim.rs` and the claim/close hot path are never touched — no git or flush work on the latency-critical dequeue path. Checkpointing cannot regress claim latency or contend with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` write transactions on the hot path.\n- **Exactly one committed path.** Only `.beads/issues.jsonl` is ever staged. `beads.db` is never staged — it is gitignored and rebuilt from JSONL via `bf sync --import`.\n- **Safe by default / opt-in.** A freshly deployed timer is inert: `bf-checkpoint.sh` prints `checkpoint disabled` and exits 0 until `checkpoint.enabled: true`. Cadence is governed by `checkpoint.interval_minutes` via a per-workspace self-throttle state file, not by how often the timer fires.\n- **Distinguishable commits.** A fixed identity (`jedarden <github@jedarden.com>`) and the `chore(beads): auto-checkpoint` prefix keep machine checkpoints separable from human commits.\n- **Push stays opt-in.** Enabled persistently by `checkpoint.push: true` or one-shot by the script's `--push` flag. The unit's `ExecStart` must never carry `--push`, which would force-push on every timer fire.\n\n**Config block** (`.beads/config.yaml`):\n\n```yaml\ncheckpoint:\n  enabled: false           # master switch; NEW ROLLOUTS STAY DISABLED until a maintainer opts in\n  interval_minutes: 60     # min gap between commits (self-throttle), default 60\n  push: false              # git push after each commit, default false\n```\n\n---\n\n## Alternative Approaches Considered\n\n### In-Memory Server (deferred)\n\nThe plan originally included a coordination server: persistent process, Unix socket protocol, `Arc<Mutex<ServerState>>`, in-memory BTreeMap priority queues, heartbeat-based stale detection. This was deferred to a future optimization because SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` delivers sufficient throughput at current scale.\n\nThe server would reduce per-claim latency from ~2ms (SQLite transaction) to ~0.1ms (memory pop). This matters only if fleets exceed 50 workers or claim frequency exceeds ~500/sec — neither is on the horizon. The server can be added transparently: `bf claim` detects the server socket, delegates if present, falls back to SQLite if not.\n\n### MCP Agent Mail (Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust)\n\nJeffrey Emanuel's companion system for inter-agent coordination. A Rust MCP server with 36 tools, 33 resources, Git-backed archive, SQLite indexing, HTTP/TUI/Robot surfaces.\n\n**Architecture**: Agents register identities, claim file reservations with TTL, exchange threaded messages, negotiate work assignments via acknowledgements. Coordination happens through conversation — \"I'm taking src/auth/**, can you work on tests/?\"\n\n**Why it doesn't fit bead-forge**: Agent Mail is built for the **pets** model — named, persistent agents that maintain identity across sessions, negotiate via messaging, and coordinate through conversation. NEEDLE uses the **cattle** model — disposable workers that are interchangeable, stateless, and need atomic dequeue without any conversation.\n\n| Aspect | Agent Mail (Pets) | bead-forge (Cattle) |\n|--------|-------------------|---------------------|\n| Agent identity | Registered, named, persistent | Anonymous, stateless, disposable |\n| Work assignment | Negotiation, messaging, agreement | Atomic SQL dequeue (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) |\n| Coordination mechanism | Threaded messages, acknowledgements | Kernel-provided mutual exclusion |\n| File/workspace ownership | Advisory file reservations | None — beads are the unit of work |\n| Communication pattern | Multi-turn conversation | Single CLI invocation |\n| Failure mode | Agent re-joins conversation | Agent dies, claim TTL expires, bead reopens |\n| Agent count | Small (3-5 named agents) | Large fleet (11-20+ disposable workers) |\n\n**What to borrow from Agent Mail**:\n- **TTL-based claim expiration**: Agent Mail uses TTL on file reservations. bead-forge applies the same concept — claims older than `claim_ttl` are reclaimed to `open` on the next claim invocation.\n\n**What to explicitly reject**:\n- **Agent identities**: Workers don't register or maintain identity. The `--assignee` field is for logging, not identity.\n- **Messaging/threading**: Workers don't send messages to each other. The only communication is claim/close through the JSONL file.\n- **File reservations**: Workers operate on entire beads, not file-level reservations.\n- **MCP layer**: bead-forge is a CLI. No stdio-based MCP protocol.\n- **Advisory locks**: Claims are enforced by `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, not advisory. Once claimed (inside the transaction), no other worker sees that bead as open.\n\n### BeadHub (juanre/beadhub)\n\nA coordination server for AI agent teams built on top of Steve Yegge's Dolt-based `bd`. The `bdh` CLI wraps `bd` and adds work claiming, file reservation, presence awareness, and inter-agent messaging. Includes a web dashboard.\n\n**Why it doesn't fit**: Tied to Dolt-based `bd` architecture (not JSONL). bead-forge needs JSONL+SQLite compatibility with br, not Dolt compatibility with bd. However, the coordination server concept validates that this problem is real and worth solving.\n\n### Beads Viewer (Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer)\n\nGraph-aware TUI with PageRank-based prioritization, critical path analysis, and kanban board view.\n\n**Why it doesn't fit**: Read-only visualization tool. Cannot perform writes (claiming, status changes). The PageRank and critical path concepts are interesting for future prioritization but don't solve the concurrency problem.\n","numLines":1777,"startLine":1,"totalLines":1777}}}

`split(';')` breaks when SQL string literals contain semicolons\n315\t/// (e.g., `INSERT INTO t(v) VALUES('a;b')`). This function uses a small state\n316\t/// machine to track whether the current position is inside:\n317\t/// - A single-quoted string literal (`'...'`, with `''` as escape)\n318\t/// - A double-quoted identifier (`\"...\"`, with `\"\"` as escape)\n319\t/// - A line comment (`-- ...`)\n320\t/// - A block comment (`/* ... */`)\n321\t///\n322\t/// Only semicolons at the top level (outside all of the above) are treated as\n323\t/// statement terminators.\n324\tfn split_sql_statements(sql: &str) -> Vec<&str> {\n325\t    let bytes = sql.as_bytes();\n326\t    let len = bytes.len();\n327\t    let mut stmts = Vec::new();\n328\t    let mut start = 0; // byte offset where the current statement begins\n329\t    let mut i = 0;\n330\t\n331\t    // State flags — at most one is true at a time.\n332\t    let mut in_single_quote = false;\n333\t    let mut in_double_quote = false;\n334\t    let mut in_line_comment = false;\n335\t    let mut in_block_comment = false;\n336\t\n337\t    while i < len {\n338\t        let b = bytes[i];\n339\t\n340\t        // --- Line comment state ---\n341\t        if in_line_comment {\n342\t            if b == b'\\n' {\n343\t                in_line_comment = false;\n344\t            }\n345\t            i += 1;\n346\t            continue;\n347\t        }\n348\t\n349\t        // --- Block comment state ---\n350\t        if in_block_comment {\n351\t            if b == b'*' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'/' {\n352\t                in_block_comment = false;\n353\t                i += 2;\n354\t            } else {\n355\t                i += 1;\n356\t            }\n357\t            continue;\n358\t        }\n359\t\n360\t        // --- Single-quoted string state ---\n361\t        if in_single_quote {\n362\t            if b == b'\\'' {\n363\t                // '' is an escaped quote inside a string literal\n364\t                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\\'' {\n365\t                    i += 2;\n366\t                } else {\n367\t                    in_single_quote = false;\n368\t                    i += 1;\n369\t                }\n370\t            } else {\n371\t                i += 1;\n372\t            }\n373\t            continue;\n374\t        }\n375\t\n376\t        // --- Double-quoted identifier state ---\n377\t        if in_double_quote {\n378\t            if b == b'\"' {\n379\t                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\"' {\n380\t                    i += 2;\n381\t                } else {\n382\t                    in_double_quote = false;\n383\t                    i += 1;\n384\t                }\n385\t            } else {\n386\t                i += 1;\n387\t            }\n388\t            continue;\n389\t        }\n390\t\n391\t        // --- Top-level parsing ---\n392\t        if b == b'\\'' {\n393\t            in_single_quote = true;\n394\t            i += 1;\n395\t        } else if b == b'\"' {\n396\t            in_double_quote = true;\n397\t            i += 1;\n398\t        } else if b == b'-' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'-' {\n399\t            in_line_comment = true;\n400\t            i += 2;\n401\t        } else if b == b'/' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'*' {\n402\t            in_block_comment = true;\n403\t            i += 2;\n404\t        } else if b == b';' {\n405\t            // Statement terminator at top level.\n406\t            let stmt = &sql[start..i];\n407\t            if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n408\t                stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n409\t            }\n410\t            start = i + 1;\n411\t            i += 1;\n412\t        } else {\n413\t            i += 1;\n414\t        }\n415\t    }\n416\t\n417\t    // Trailing statement without a final semicolon.\n418\t    if start < len {\n419\t        let stmt = &sql[start..len];\n420\t        if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n421\t            stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n422\t        }\n423\t    }\n424\t\n425\t    stmts\n426\t}\n427\t\n428\t/// Execute multiple SQL statements separated by semicolons.\n429\tfn execute_batch(conn: &Connection, sql: &str) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n430\t    conn.execute_batch(sql)?;\n431\t    Ok(())\n432\t}\n433\t\n434\tpub fn apply_schema(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n435\t    execute_batch(conn, SCHEMA_SQL)?;\n436\t    apply_migrations(conn)?;\n437\t identifiers, and comments.\n///\n/// A naive `split(';')` breaks when SQL string literals contain semicolons\n/// (e.g., `INSERT INTO t(v) VALUES('a;b')`). This function uses a small state\n/// machine to track whether the current position is inside:\n/// - A single-quoted string literal (`'...'`, with `''` as escape)\n/// - A double-quoted identifier (`\"...\"`, with `\"\"` as escape)\n/// - A line comment (`-- ...`)\n/// - A block comment (`/* ... */`)\n///\n/// Only semicolons at the top level (outside all of the above) are treated as\n/// statement terminators.\nfn split_sql_statements(sql: &str) -> Vec<&str> {\n    let bytes = sql.as_bytes();\n    let len = bytes.len();\n    let mut stmts = Vec::new();\n    let mut start = 0; // byte offset where the current statement begins\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    // State flags — at most one is true at a time.\n    let mut in_single_quote = false;\n    let mut in_double_quote = false;\n    let mut in_line_comment = false;\n    let mut in_block_comment = false;\n\n    while i < len {\n        let b = bytes[i];\n\n        // --- Line comment state ---\n        if in_line_comment {\n            if b == b'\\n' {\n                in_line_comment = false;\n            }\n            i += 1;\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Block comment state ---\n        if in_block_comment {\n            if b == b'*' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'/' {\n                in_block_comment = false;\n                i += 2;\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Single-quoted string state ---\n        if in_single_quote {\n            if b == b'\\'' {\n                // '' is an escaped quote inside a string literal\n                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\\'' {\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    in_single_quote = false;\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Double-quoted identifier state ---\n        if in_double_quote {\n            if b == b'\"' {\n                if i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'\"' {\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    in_double_quote = false;\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // --- Top-level parsing ---\n        if b == b'\\'' {\n            in_single_quote = true;\n            i += 1;\n        } else if b == b'\"' {\n            in_double_quote = true;\n            i += 1;\n        } else if b == b'-' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'-' {\n            in_line_comment = true;\n            i += 2;\n        } else if b == b'/' && i + 1 < len && bytes[i + 1] == b'*' {\n            in_block_comment = true;\n            i += 2;\n        } else if b == b';' {\n            // Statement terminator at top level.\n            let stmt = &sql[start..i];\n            if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n                stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n            }\n            start = i + 1;\n            i += 1;\n        } else {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Trailing statement without a final semicolon.\n    if start < len {\n        let stmt = &sql[start..len];\n        if !stmt.trim().is_empty() {\n            stmts.push(stmt.trim());\n        }\n    }\n\n    stmts\n}\n\n/// Execute multiple SQL statements separated by semicolons.\nfn execute_batch(conn: &Connection, sql: &str) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    conn.execute_batch(sql)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\npub fn apply_schema(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    execute_batch(conn, SCHEMA_SQL)?;\n    apply_migrations(conn)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Apply database migrations for schema changes.\n/// This handles adding new columns to existing tables.\nfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    // Migration 1: Update critical_path_cache schema if it has the old format\n    // Old format: bead_id, float (REAL), updated_at\n    // New format: bead_id, epic_id, es (INTEGER), ls (INTEGER), float (INTEGER), updated_at\n    let has_es: bool = conn\n        .query_row(\n            \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('critical_path_cache') WHERE name='es'\",\n            [],\n            |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0).map(|n| n > 0),\n        )\n        .unwrap_or(false);\n\n    if !has_es {\n        // Table has old schema - recreate with new schema\n        conn.execute_batch(\n            \"BEGIN;\n             CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS critical_path_cache_new (\n                 bead_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n                 epic_id     TEXT,\n                 es          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n                 ls          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n             );\n             INSERT INTO critical_path_cache_new (bead_id, float, updated_at)\n                 SELECT bead_id, CAST(float AS INTEGER), updated_at FROM critical_path_cache;\n             DROP TABLE critical_path_cache;\n             ALTER TABLE critical_path_cache_new RENAME TO critical_path_cache;\n             COMMIT;\",\n        )?;\n    }\n\n    // Create indexes for critical_path_cache (idempotent)\n    let _ = conn.execute_batch(\n        \"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_critical_path_cache_epic ON critical_path_cache(epic_id);\n         CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_critical_path_cache_float ON critical_path_cache(float);\",\n    );\n\n    // Migration 2: Add workspace_path to worker_sessions if missing\n    // Older databases may not have this column;     \"ALTER TABLE worker_sessions ADD COLUMN workspace_path TEXT\",\n            [],\n        )?;\n    }\n\n    // Migration 3: Add closed_at and duration_seconds to worker_sessions for velocity tracking\n    let has_closed_at: bool = conn\n        .query_row(\n            \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('worker_sessions') WHERE name='closed_at'\",\n            [],\n            |row| DATETIME\",\n            [],\n        )?;\n        conn.execute(\n            \"ALTER TABLE worker_sessions ADD COLUMN duration_seconds INTEGER\",\n            [],\n        )?;\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\npub fn ensure_wal_mode(conn: &Connection) -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n    // Use execute_batch so PRAGMAs that return rows don't cause errors\n    conn.execute_batch(\n        \"PRAGMA drift.missing_in_jsonl.is_empty() {\n314\t            // Only report unflushed if not already covered by DbNewer\n315\t            anomalies.push(Anomaly::new(\n316\t                AnomalyClass::Unflushed,\n317\t                format!(\"{} unflushed bead(s) exist\", unflushed_count),\n318\t            ));\n319\t        }\n320\t    }\n321\t\n322\t    // Check for beads stuck in pseudo-terminal status\n323\t    let pseudo_terminal_ids = check_pseudo_terminal_statuses(&db_path)?;\n324\t    if !pseudo_terminal_ids.is_empty() {\n325\t        anomalies.push(\n326\t            Anomaly::new(\n327\t                AnomalyClass::PseudoTerminal,\n328\t                format!(\"{} bead(s) have done-sounding status instead of closed\", pseudo_terminal_ids.len()),\n329\t            )\n330\t            .with_ids(pseudo_terminal_ids.clone()),\n331\t        );\n332\t    }\n333\t    result.pseudo_terminal_status_ids = pseudo_terminal_ids;\n334\t\n335\t    // Check for beads stuck in blocked status\n336\t    let stale_blocked_ids = check_stale_blocked_statuses(&db_path)?;\n337\t    if !stale_blocked_ids.is_empty() {\n338\t        anomalies.push(\n339\t            Anomaly::new(\n340\t                AnomalyClass::StaleBlocked,\n341\t                format!(\"{} bead(s) stuck in blocked status\", stale_blocked_ids.len()),\n342\t            )\n343\t            .with_ids(stale_blocked_ids.clone()),\n344\t        );\n345\t    }\n346\t    result.stale_blocked_ids = stale_blocked_ids;\n347\t\n348\t    // Check for NULL in NOT NULL columns\n349\t    let null_not_null = check_null_not_null(&db_path)?;\n350\t    if !null_not_null.is_empty() {\n351\t        let total: usize = null_not_null.iter().map(|v| v.count).sum();\n352\t        let detail = null_not_null\n353\t            .iter()\n354\t            .map(|v| format!(\"{}.{}\", v.table, v.column))\n355\t            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n356\t            .join(\", \");\n357\t        anomalies.push(\n358\t            Anomaly::new(\n359\t                AnomalyClass::NullNotNull,\n360\t                format!(\"{} NULL value(s) in NOT NULL columns: {}\", total, detail),\n361\t            )\n362\t            .with_context(format!(\"{:?}\", null_not_null)),\n363\t        );\n364\t    }\n365\t    result.null_not_null = null_not_null;\n366\t\n367\t    result.db_ok = db_ok;\n368\t    result.jsonl_ok = jsonl_ok;\n369\t    result.healthy = anomalies.is_empty() && db_ok && jsonl_ok;\n370\t    result.anomalies = anomalies;\n371\t\n372\t    Ok(result)\n373\t}\n374\t\n375\t/// Find beads whose status is 'blocked' but have no active (non-terminal) blockers.\n376\t/// These are stale 'blocked' beads that should be 'open' but were never transitioned\n377\t/// when their last blocker closed (bf-5id).\n378\tfn check_stale_blocked_statuses(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n379\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n380\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n381\t\n382\t    // Find beads where:\n383\t    // 1. status = 'blocked'\n384\t    // 2. NOT deleted\n385\t    // 3. COUNT of active blockers (non-terminal status) = 0\n386\t    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(\n387\t        r#\"\n388\t        SELECT i.id\n389\t        FROM issues i\n390\t        WHERE i.status = 'blocked'\n391\t        AND i.deleted_at IS NULL\n392\t        AND (\n393\t            SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.depends_on_id)\n394\t            FROM dependencies d\n395\t            INNER JOIN issues blocker ON blocker.id = d.depends_on_id\n396\t            WHERE d.issue_id = i.id\n397\t            AND d.type IN ('blocks', 'parent-child', 'conditional-blocks', 'waits-for')\n398\t            AND blocker.status NOT IN ('closed', 'tombstone', 'done', 'completed')\n399\t        ) = 0\n400\t        ORDER BY i.id\n401\t        \"#\n402\t    )?;\n403\t\n404\t    let ids = stmt\n405\t        .query_map([], |row| row.get::<_, String>(0))?\n406\t        .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;\n407\t    Ok(ids)\n408\t}\n409\t\n410\t/// Find beads whose status is a `TERMINAL_STATUS_ALIASES` value (e.g. \"completed\",\n411\t/// \"done\") rather than the canonical \"closed\"/\"tombstone\". These beads are functionally\n412\t/// terminal (see `Status::is_terminal()`) but weren't actually closed, so `bf show`/`bf\n413\t/// list` still displays them as active and `closed_at`/`close_reason` are never set.\n414\tfn check_pseudo_terminal_statuses(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n415\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n416\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n417\t    let placeholders = crate::model::TERMINAL_STATUS_ALIASES\n418\t        .iter()\n419\t        .map(|s| format!(\"'{s}'\"))\n420\t        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n421\t        .join(\", \");\n422\t    let query = format!(\n423\t        \"SELECT id FROM issues WHERE LOWER(status) IN ({placeholders}) AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY id\"\n424\t    );\n425\t    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(&query)?;\n426\t    let ids = stmt\n427\t        .query_map([], |row| row.get::<_, String>(0))?\n428\t        .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;\n429\t    Ok(ids)\n430\t}\n431\t\n432\t/// List the user tables in the database (excluding SQLite internal tables).\n433\tfn user_tables(conn: &Connection) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n434\t    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(\n435\t        \"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY name\",\n436\t    )?;\n437\t    let tables = stmt\n438\t        .query_map([], |row| row.get::<_, String>(0))?\n439\t        .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;\n440\t    Ok(tables)\n441\t}\n442\t\n443\t/// A NOT NULL column, discovered by introspecting the live schema.\n444\tstruct NotNullColumn {\n445\t    table: String,\n446\t    column: String,\n447\t    decl_type: String,\n448\t}\n449\t\n450\t/// Introspect every user table via `PRAGMA table_info` and return the columns the\n451\t/// schema declares NOT NULL. Driving off the live schema (rather than a hardcoded\n452\t/// list) keeps the detector and fixer correct as the schema evolves -- this is the\n453\t/// \"generally\" in \"NULL-in-NOT-NULL rows generally\" (bf-3hm5h).\n454\tfn not_null_columns(conn: &Connection) -> Result<Vec<NotNullColumn>> {\n455\t    let mut cols = Vec::new();\n456\t    for table in user_tables(conn)? {\n457\t        // PRAGMA table_info columns: cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk\n458\t        let mut stmt = conn.prepare(&format!(\"PRAGMA table_info(\\\"{}\\\")\", table.replace('\"', \"\\\"\\\"\")))?;\n459\t        let rows = stmt\n460\t            .query_map([], |row| {\n461\t                let name: String = row.get(1)?;\n462\t                let decl_type: String = row.get(2)?;\n463\t                let notnull: i64 = row.get(3)?;\n464\t                Ok((name, decl_type, notnull))\n465\t            })?\n466\t            .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;\n467\t        for (name, decl_type, notnull) in rows {\n468\t            if notnull == 1 {\n469\t                cols.push(NotNullColumn {\n470\t                    table: table.clone(),\n471\t                    column: name,\n472\t                    decl_type,\n473\t                });\n474\t            }\n475\t        }\n476\t    }\n477\t    Ok(cols)\n478\t}\n479\t\n480\t/// Quote a SQLite identifier (table or column name) for safe interpolation.\n481\tfn quote_ident(name: &str) -> String {\n482\t    format!(\"\\\"{}\\\"\", name.replace('\"', \"\\\"\\\"\"))\n483\t}\n484\t\n485\t/// Detect rows storing NULL in a NOT NULL column (bf-3hm5h).\n486\t///\n487\t/// The schema forbids this, but corrupted databases have contained it -- most\n488\t/// notably a NULL `created_at`/`updated_at` that turned every `bf list`/`bf flush`\n489\t/// into a fatal `InvalidColumnType` crash. Reads are now NULL-tolerant; this\n490\t/// detector surfaces the underlying rows so `fix_null_not_null` can repair them.\n491\tfn check_null_not_null(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<NullNotNullViolation>> {\n492\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n493\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n494\t\n495\t    let mut violations = Vec::new();\n496\t    for col in not_null_columns(&conn)? {\n497\t        // NOTE: test `typeof(col) = 'null'`, NOT `col IS NULL`. SQLite's query planner\n498\t        // assumes a NOT NULL column never holds NULL and folds `col IS NULL` to a\n499\t        // constant FALSE -- so `IS NULL` can *never* surface this corruption. `typeof()`\n500\t        // forces per-row evaluation and reports 'null' for a stored NULL regardless of\n501\t        // the column's declared constraint.\n502\t        let count: i64 = conn.query_row(\n503\t            &format!(\n504\t                \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {} WHERE typeof({}) = 'null'\",\n505\t                quote_ident(&col.table),\n506\t                quote_ident(&col.column)\n507\t            ),\n508\t            [],\n509\t            |row| row.get(0),\n510\t        )?;\n511\t        if count > 0 {\n512\t            violations.push(NullNotNullViolation {\n513\t                table: col.table,\n514\t                column: col.column,\n515\t                decl_type: col.decl_type,\n516\t                count: count as usize,\n517\t            });\n518\t        }\n519\t    }\n520\t    Ok(violations)\n521\t}\n522\t\n523\t/// Repair rows that store NULL in a NOT NULL column, in place (bf-3hm5h).\n524\t///\n525\t/// This is a non-destructive fixer -- unlike `repair`, it does not rebuild from\n526\t/// JSONL, so it works even when JSONL is absent or itself suspect, and it never\n527\t/// touches valid rows. Each NULL is replaced with a type-appropriate sentinel:\n528\t///\n529\t/// * `DATETIME` columns -> the Unix epoch (`1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00`), matching\n530\t///   the value NULL-tolerant reads already substitute, so a fixed row round-trips\n531\t///   identically to how it was already being displayed.\n532\t/// * `INTEGER`/`REAL`/numeric columns -> `0`.\n533\t/// * everything else (TEXT/BLOB) -> the empty string, matching the schema's\n534\t///   `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` convention for text columns.\n535\t///\n536\t/// Returns the total number of column values updated.\n537\tpub fn fix_null_not_null(workspace_dir: &Path) -> Result<usize> {\n538\t    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n539\t        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n540\t    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n541\t    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n542\t\n543\t    let violations = check_null_not_null(&db_path)?;\n544\t    if violations.is_empty() {\n545\t        return Ok(0);\n546\t    }\n547\t\n548\t    let conn = Connection::open(&db_path)?;\n549\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n550\t\n551\t    let mut fixed = 0usize;\n552\t    for v in &violations {\n553\t        let upper = v.decl_type.to_uppercase();\n554\t        // SQLite type affinity: DATE/TIME columns first (they must not be caught by\n555\t        // the INT affinity rule below), then numeric, then everything else.\n556\t        let replacement = if upper.contains(\"DATE\") || upper.contains(\"TIME\") {\n557\t            \"'1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'\".to_string()\n558\t        } else if upper.contains(\"INT\")\n559\t            || upper.contains(\"REAL\")\n560\t            || upper.contains(\"FLOA\")\n561\t            || upper.contains(\"DOUB\")\n562\t            || upper.contains(\"NUM\")\n563\t            || upper.contains(\"DEC\")\n564\t        {\n565\t            \"0\".to_string()\n566\t        } else {\n567\t            \"''\".to_string()\n568\t        };\n569\t\n570\t        // `typeof(col) = 'null'`, NOT `col IS NULL`: the planner folds `IS NULL` on a\n571\t        // NOT NULL column to FALSE, so an `IS NULL` UPDATE would silently match zero\n572\t        // rows and \"repair\" nothing. See check_null_not_null for the full rationale.\n573\t        let updated = conn.execute(\n574\t            &format!(\n575\t                \"UPDATE {} SET {} = {} WHERE typeof({}) = 'null'\",\n576\t                quote_ident(&v.table),\n577\t                quote_ident(&v.column),\n578\t                replacement,\n579\t                quote_ident(&v.column)\n580\t            ),\n581\t            [],\n582\t        )?;\n583\t        fixed += updated;\n584\t    }\n585\t\n586\t    Ok(fixed)\n587\t}\n588\t\n589\t/// Check database integrity.\n590\tfn check_database(db_path: &Path) -> Result<(usize, bool)> {\n591\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n592\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n593\t\n594\t    // Apply schema if database is new (no tables yet)\n595\t    let needs_schema: bool = conn\n596\t        .query_row(\n597\t            \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='issues'\",\n598\t            [],\n599\t            |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0),\n600\t        )\n601\t        .map(|n| n == 0)\n602\t        .unwrap_or(true);\n603\t    if needs_schema {\n604\t        crate::storage::schema::apply_schema(&conn)?;\n605\t    }\n606\t\n607\t    // Run PRAGMA integrity_check\n608\t    let integrity_result: String =\n609\t        conn.query_row(\"PRAGMA integrity_check\", [], |row| row.get(0))?;\n610\t\n611\t    let integrity_ok = integrity_result == \"ok\";\n612\t\n613\t    // Count issues\n614\t    let count: i64 = conn.query_row(\n615\t        \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM issues WHERE deleted_at IS NULL\",\n616\t        [],\n617\t        |row| row.get(0),\n618\t    )?;\n619\t\n620\t    Ok((count as usize, integrity_ok))\n621\t}\n622\t\n623\t/// Check JSONL file validity.\n624\tfn check_jsonl(jsonl_path: &Path) -> Result<(usize, bool)> {\n625\t    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n626\t        return Ok((0, true)); // Empty workspace is valid\n627\t    }\n628\t\n629\t    let mut count = 0;\n630\t    let mut valid = true;\n631\t\n632\t    match stream_issues(jsonl_path) {\n633\t        Ok(iter) => {\n634\t            for result in iter {\n635\t                match result {\n636\t                    Ok(_) => count += 1,\n637\t                    Err(e) => {\n638\t                        valid = false;\n639\t                        eprintln!(\"Invalid JSONL line: {}\", e);\n640\t                    }\n641\t                }\n642\t            }\n643\t        }\n644\t        Err(e) => {\n645\t            return Err(anyhow!(\"Failed to read JSONL file: {}\", e));\n646\t        }\n647\t    }\n648\t\n649\t    Ok((count, valid))\n650\t}\n651\t\n652\t/// Consistency drift details.\n653\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n654\tstruct ConsistencyDrift {\n655\t    /// Bead IDs that exist in SQLite but not in JSONL\n656\t    missing_in_jsonl: Vec<String>,\n657\t    /// Bead IDs that exist in JSONL but not in SQLite\n658\t    missing_in_sqlite: Vec<String>,\n659\t    /// Bead IDs where content_hash differs between JSONL and SQLite\n660\t    hash_mismatch: Vec<String>,\n661\t}\n662\t\n663\t/// Check consistency between database and JSONL using content_hash.\n664\t///\n665\t/// Compares each bead's content_hash between JSONL and SQLite to detect drift.\n666\tfn check_consistency_with_hash(db_path: &Path, jsonl_path: &Path) -> Result<ConsistencyDrift> {\n667\t    use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\n668\t\n669\t    let storage = Storage::open(db_path)?;\n670\t\n671\t    // Build a map of all SQLite issues with their content_hash\n672\t    let sqlite_issues: HashMap<String, String> = storage\n673\t        .list_all_issues()?\n674\t        .into_iter()\n675\t        .map(|issue| {\n676\t            let hash = issue.content_hash();\n677\t            (issue.id, hash)\n678\t        })\n679\t        .collect();\n680\t\n681\t    let mut drift = ConsistencyDrift::default();\n682\t    let mut jsonl_seen: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n683\t\n684\t    // Stream JSONL and compare, tracking seen IDs\n685\t    if jsonl_path.exists() {\n686\t        let iter = stream_issues(jsonl_path)?;\n687\t        for result in iter {\n688\t            let jsonl_issue = result?;\n689\t            let jsonl_hash = jsonl_issue.content_hash();\n690\t            let bead_id = jsonl_issue.id.clone();\n691\t            jsonl_seen.insert(bead_id.clone());\n692\t\n693\t            match sqlite_issues.get(&bead_id) {\n694\t                Some(sqlite_hash) => {\n695\t                    if sqlite_hash != &jsonl_hash {\n696\t                        drift.hash_mismatch.push(bead_id);\n697\t                    }\n698\t                }\n699\t                None => {\n700\t                    drift.missing_in_sqlite.push(bead_id);\n701\t                }\n702\t            }\n703\t        }\n704\t    }\n705\t\n706\t    // Find beads in SQLite but not in JSONL (using tracked seen IDs)\n707\t    for bead_id in sqlite_issues.keys() {\n708\t        if !jsonl_seen.contains(bead_id) {\n709\t            drift.missing_in_jsonl.push(bead_id.clone());\n710\t        }\n711\t    }\n712\t\n713\t    Ok(drift)\n714\t}\n715\t\n716\t/// Count unflushed beads (db-only or db-newer beads not yet flushed to JSONL).\n717\t///\n718\t/// Returns the count of beads that exist in SQLite but have been marked as dirty\n719\t/// (modified or created since the last flush to JSONL).\n720\tpub fn count_unflushed(db_path: &Path) -> Result<usize> {\n721\t    use rusqlite::Connection;\n722\t\n723\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n724\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n725\t\n726\t    // Check if dirty_issues table exists\n727\t    let table_exists: i64 = conn.query_row(\n728\t        \"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='dirty_issues'\",\n729\t        [],\n730\t        |row| row.get(0),\n731\t    )?;\n732\t\n733\t    if table_exists == 0 {\n734\t        return Ok(0);\n735\t    }\n736\t\n737\t    let count: i64 = conn.query_row(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dirty_issues\", [], |row| row.get(0))?;\n738\t\n739\t    Ok(count as usize)\n740\t}\n741\t\n742\t/// Get IDs of unflushed beads.\n743\t///\n744\t/// Returns a list of bead IDs that exist in SQLite but have been marked as dirty\n745\t/// (modified or created since the last flush to JSONL).\n746\tfn get_unflushed_ids(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n747\t    use rusqlite::Connection;\n748\t\n749\t    let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n750\t    conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n751\t\n752\t    // Check if dirty_issues table exists\n753\t    let table_exists: i64 = table_exists == 0 {\n760\t        return Ok(Vec::new());\n761\t    }\n762\t\n763\t    let mut stmt = conn.prepare(\"SELECT issue_id FROM dirty_issues ORDER BY issue_id\")?;\n764\t    let mut rows = stmt.query([])?;\n765\t\n766\t    let mut ids = Vec::new();\n767\t    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {\n768\t        ids.push(row.get(0)?);\n769\t    }\n770\t\n771\t    Ok(ids)\n772\t}\n773\t\n774\t/// Repair the database by rebuilding from JSONL.\n775\t///\n776\t/// This is the recovery operation when the database is corrupted or missing.\n777\t/// The JSONL file is the authoritative source of truth for repair.\n778\t///\n779\t/// # Arguments\n780\t/// * `workspace_dir` - Path to the workspace root (contains .beads/)\n781\t/// * `flush_first` - If true, flush unflushed beads to JSONL before repairing\n782\t/// * `force` - If true, proceed even with unflushed beads (they will be lost)\n783\t///\n784\t/// # Returns\n785\t/// * `Ok(usize)` - Number of beads imported\n786\tpub fn repair(workspace_dir: &Path, flush_first: bool, force: bool) -> Result<usize> {\n787\t    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n788\t        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n789\t    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n790\t    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n791\t    let jsonl_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.jsonl_export);\n792\t\n793\t    // Check if JSONL exists\n794\t    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n795\t        return Err(anyhow!(\n796\t            \"Cannot repair: JSONL file not found at {}\",\n797\t            jsonl_path.display()\n798\t        ));\n799\t    }\n800\t\n801\t    // Check for unflushed beads if database exists and is valid\n802\t    // If db is corrupted, we can't detect unflushed beads - proceed with warning\n803\t    let (unflushed_ids, db_corrupted) = if db_path.exists() {\n804\t        match get_unflushed_ids(&db_path) {\n805\t            Ok(ids) => (ids, false),\n806\t            Err(_) => {\n807\t                // Database is corrupted or unreadable\n808\t                // We can't detect unflushed beads, so proceed with a warning\n809\t                if flush_first {\n810\t                    // Cannot flush from a corrupt database\n811\t                    return Err(anyhow!(\n812\t                        \"Cannot flush: database is corrupted and unreadable.\\n\\\n813\t                         Flushing from a corrupt DB would poison the JSONL checkpoint.\\n\\\n814\t                         Unflushed beads cannot be recovered.\\n\\\n815\t                         Remove --flush-first to proceed with repair only.\"\n816\t                    ));\n817\t                }\n818\t                // Proceed without unflushed check (db is unreadable)\n819\t                // No --force needed since we can't detect unflushed beads anyway\n820\t                eprintln!(\"WARNING: Database is corrupted and unreadable.\");\n821\t                eprintln!(\"  Cannot detect unflushed beads - any db-only beads will be lost.\");\n822\t                eprintln!(\"  Proceeding with repair from JSONL...\");\n823\t                (Vec::new(), true)\n824\t            }\n825\t        }\n826\t    } else {\n827\t        // DB doesn't exist - no unflushed beads possible\n828\t        (Vec::new(), false)\n829\t    };\n830\t\n831\t    if !unflushed_ids.is_empty() {\n832\t        if flush_first {\n833\t            // Flush ALL beads to JSONL first (not just dirty ones)\n834\t            // We must export everything because repair will rebuild db from JSONL\n835\t            eprintln!(\n836\t                \"Flushing all beads to JSONL before repair (including {} unflushed)...\",\n837\t                unflushed_ids.len()\n838\t            );\n839\t            let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n840\t            let flushed = storage.sync_to_jsonl(&jsonl_path, false)?;\n841\t            eprintln!(\"Flushed {} bead(s) to JSONL\", flushed);\n842\t        } else if !force {\n843\t            // Refuse to proceed with unflushed beads\n844\t            return Err(anyhow!(\n845\t                \"Cannot repair: {} unflushed bead(s) exist ({}).\\n\\\n846\t                 Run 'bf doctor --repair --flush-first' to flush before repair,\\n\\\n847\t                 or 'bf doctor --repair --force' to proceed (these beads will be LOST).\\n\\\n848\t                 Unflushed beads: {}\",\n849\t                unflushed_ids.len(),\n850\t                if unflushed_ids.len() <= 5 {\n851\t                    unflushed_ids.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\", \")\n852\t                } else {\n853\t                    format!(\n854\t                        \"{}, ... and {} more\",\n855\t                        unflushed_ids[..5].join(\", \"),\n856\t                        unflushed_ids.len() - 5\n857\t                    )\n858\t                },\n859\t                unflushed_ids.join(\", \")\n860\t            ));\n861\t        } else {\n862\t            // Force mode: warn but proceed\n863\t            eprintln!(\n864\t                \"WARNING: {} unflushed bead(s) will be LOST: {}\",\n865\t                unflushed_ids.len(),\n866\t                if unflushed_ids.len() <= 5 {\n867\t                    unflushed_ids.iter().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\", \")\n868\t                } else {\n869\t                    format!(\n870\t                        \"{}, ... and {} more\",\n871\t                        unflushed_ids[..5].join(\", \"),\n872\t                        unflushed_ids.len() - 5\n873\t                    )\n874\t                }\n875\t            );\n876\t            eprintln!(\"Proceeding with repair due to --force flag\");\n877\t        }\n878\t    }\n879\t\n880\t    // Backup existing database if it exists\n881\t    if db_path.exists() {\n882\t        let &backup_path)?;\n887\t        eprintln!(\"Backed up existing database to {}\", backup_path.display());\n888\t    }\n889\t\n890\t    // Delete old database\n891\t    if db_path.exists() {\n892\t        std::fs::remove_file(&db_path)?;\n893\t    }\n894\t\n895\t    // Create new database and import JSONL\n896\t    let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n897\t\n898\t    let result = storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n899\t        import_jsonl(&jsonl_path, |issue| {\n900\t            Storage::create_issue_tx(tx, &issue)?;\n901\t            Ok(UpsertResult::New)\n902\t sync\n909\t    // (create_issue_tx doesn't mark dirty, but we clear for safety)\n910\t    storage.clear_dirty()?;\n911\t\n912\t    Ok(result.imported)\n913\t}\n914\t\n915\t// ===========================================================================\n916\t// Doctor safety stack (Phase 7.2 — layered repair + beads_rust#394 preservation)\n917\t//\n918\t// `repair_stack` is the user-facing `bf doctor --repair` path. Unlike the\n919\t// low-level `repair` primitive above (which unconditionally rebuilds from JSONL),\n920\t// it walks a layered safety architecture and only reaches the destructive JSONL\n921\t// rebuild as a last resort, always behind a verified restorable backup:\n922\t//\n923\t//   1. Healthy early-return  — a workspace with no corruption/divergence never\n924\t//      rebuilds; only trivial, non-destructive fixers run.\n925\t//   2. Local repair first    — integrity triage + VACUUM/REINDEX/cache rebuild;\n926\t//      if that resolves the problem, the JSONL rebuild is never reached.\n927\t//   3. Verified backups      — SHA-256-hashed copies of the DB family + JSONL into\n928\t//      `.beads/recovery/<run-id>/` before any rebuild; restore-on-failure.\n929\t//   4. JSONL authority preflight — refuse rebuild if the JSONL carries merge\n930\t//      conflict markers or unparseable records (never rebuild from a poisoned\n931\t//      authority).\n932\t//   5. Repeat-failure gate   — a rebuild that fails post-verification writes a\n933\t//      marker; further rebuilds refuse without `--allow-repeated-repair`.\n934\t//   6. Preservation across rebuild (beads_rust#394) — snapshot unflushed dirty\n935\t//      issues (with labels/deps/comments) *and* tombstones before the rebuild,\n936\t//      restore + re-mark them dirty after, and report the preserved count.\n937\t// ===========================================================================\n938\t\n939\t/// Options controlling a layered `repair_stack` run.\n940\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n941\tpub struct RepairOptions {\n942\t    /// Flush unflushed (dirty) beads to JSONL before rebuild.\n943\t    pub flush_first: bool,\n944\t    /// Discard unflushed dirty beads instead of preserving them across a rebuild.\n945\t    /// Preservation is the default; `force` opts out (the legacy destructive path).\n946\t    pub force: bool,\n947\t    /// Proceed even if a prior rebuild left a repeat-failure marker (layer 5).\n948\t    pub allow_repeated_repair: bool,\n949\t}\n950\t\n951\t/// Structured outcome of a layered `repair_stack` run.\n952\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n953\tpub struct RepairReport {\n954\t    /// True when the workspace was healthy (or locally repairable) and no JSONL\n955\t    /// rebuild was performed.\n956\t    pub healthy: bool,\n957\t    /// True when a JSONL rebuild was performed.\n958\t    pub rebuilt: bool,\n959\t    /// Beads imported from JSONL during a rebuild (0 if no rebuild).\n960\t    pub imported: usize,\n961\t    /// Unflushed dirty beads snapshotted and restored across the rebuild (layer 6).\n962\t    pub preserved_dirty: usize,\n963\t    /// Non-destructive local fixers that were applied (layer 2).\n964\t    pub local_fixes: Vec<String>,\n965\t    /// Run id of the verified pre-rebuild backup (layer 3), if a rebuild ran.\n966\t    pub backup_run_id: Option<String>,\n967\t    /// Human-readable notes for the CLI summary.\n968\t    pub messages: Vec<String>,\n969\t}\n970\t\n971\t/// Resolve the `.beads` dir + db/jsonl paths for a workspace.\n972\tfn resolve_paths(workspace_dir: &Path) -> Result<(PathBuf, PathBuf, PathBuf)> {\n973\t    let beads_dir = find_beads_dir(workspace_dir)\n974\t        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"No .beads directory found in {}\", workspace_dir.display()))?;\n975\t    let metadata = load_metadata(&beads_dir)?;\n976\t    let db_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.database);\n977\t    let jsonl_path = beads_dir.join(&metadata.jsonl_export);\n978\t    Ok((beads_dir, db_path, jsonl_path))\n979\t}\n980\t\n981\t/// The DB family + JSONL authority paths that a pre-rebuild backup captures.\n982\tfn backup_targets(db_path: &Path, jsonl_path: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {\n983\t    let db_str = db_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();\n984\t    vec![\n985\t        db_path.to_path_buf(),\n986\t        PathBuf::from(format!(\"{}-wal\", db_str)),\n987\t        PathBuf::from(format!(\"{}-shm\", db_str)),\n988\t        jsonl_path.to_path_buf(),\n989\t    ]\n990\t}\n991\t\n992\t/// Layer 4 — JSONL authority preflight.\n993\t///\n994\t/// Refuse to treat the JSONL as authoritative for a rebuild if it contains git\n995\t/// merge-conflict markers or any unparseable record. Rebuilding from a poisoned\n996\t/// authority is exactly how a bad flush or a botched merge becomes permanent.\n997\tpub fn preflight_jsonl(jsonl_path: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n998\t    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n999\t        return Ok(()); // A fresh/empty workspace has nothing to poison.\n1000\t    }\n1001\t\n1002\t    // Scan raw lines for conflict markers first — these produce the clearest error.\n1003\t    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(jsonl_path)\n1004\t        .map_err(|e| anyhow!(\"Cannot read JSONL for preflight: {}\", e))?;\n1005\t    for (idx, line) in content.lines().enumerate() {\n1006\t        if line.starts_with(\"<<<<<<<\")\n1007\t            || line.starts_with(\">>>>>>>\")\n1008\t            || line == \"=======\"\n1009\t            || line.starts_with(\"======= \")\n1010\t            || line.starts_with(\"|||||||\")\n1011\t        {\n1012\t            return Err(anyhow!(\n1013\t                \"Refusing to rebuild: JSONL contains a git merge-conflict marker at line {} \\\n1014\t                 (\\\"{}\\\"). A single invalid record means the JSONL is\n1024\t    // not a trustworthy authority for a full rebuild.\n1025\t    let mut invalid = Vec::new();\n1026\t    for (idx, result) in stream_issues(jsonl_path)?.enumerate() {\n1027\t        if let Err(e) = result {\n1028\t            invalid.push(format!(\"line {}: {}\", idx + 1, e));\n1029\t            if invalid.len() >= 5 {\n1030\t                break;\n1031\t            }\n1032\t        }\n1033\t    }\n1034\t    if !invalid.is_empty() {\n1035\t        return Err(anyhow!(\n1036\t            \"Refusing to rebuild: JSONL contains {} invalid record(s) [{}]. \\\n1037\t             Fix or remove the bad lines in {} before repairing.\",\n1038\t            invalid.len(),\n1039\t            invalid.join(\"; \"),\n1040\t            jsonl_path.display()\n1041\t        ));\n1042\t    }\n1043\t\n1044\t    Ok(())\n1045\t}\n1046\t\n1047\t/// Layer 2 — non-destructive local repair.\n1048\t///\n1049\t/// Runs integrity triage and cheap local recovery (VACUUM, REINDEX, blocked-cache\n1050\t/// rebuild). Returns the list of fixers applied. Never touches JSONL and never\n1051\t/// drops data; safe to run on any openable database.\n1052\tfn local_repair(db_path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n1053\t    let mut applied = Vec::new();\n1054\t    if !db_path.exists() {\n1055\t        return Ok(applied);\n1056\t    }\n1057\t\n1058\t    {\n1059\t        let conn = Connection::open(db_path)?;\n1060\t        conn.busy_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))?;\n1061\t        // VACUUM compacts and can clear certain free-list inconsistencies.\n1062\t        conn.execute_batch(\"VACUUM\")?;\n1063\t        applied.push(\"VACUUM\".to_string());\n1064\t        // REINDEX rebuilds every index from the (authoritative) table rows.\n1065\t        conn.execute_batch(\"REINDEX\")?;\n1066\t        applied.push(\"REINDEX\".to_string());\n1067\t    }\n1068\t\n1069\t    // Rebuild the derived blocked-issues cache from the live graph.\n1070\t    let storage = Storage::open(db_path)?;\n1071\t    storage.rebuild_blocked_cache()?;\n1072\t    applied.push(\"rebuild-blocked-cache\".to_string());\n1073\t\n1074\t    Ok(applied)\n1075\t}\n1076\t\n1077\t/// Core rebuild used by the safety stack: replace the DB by importing from JSONL.\n1078\t///\n1079\t/// Unlike the `repair` primitive, this performs no dirty-bead guard and writes no\n1080\t/// ad-hoc `.db.backup.*` file — the layered caller has already taken a verified\n1081\t/// recovery backup and captured any dirty state to restore afterwards.\n1082\tfn rebuild_db_from_jsonl(db_path: &Path, jsonl_path: &Path) -> Result<usize> {\n1083\t    if db_path.exists() {\n1084\t        std::fs::remove_file(db_path)?;\n1085\t    }\n1086\t    // Remove stale SQLite sidecars so the fresh DB starts clean.\n1087\t    for sidecar in [\"-wal\", \"-shm\"] {\n1088\t        let p = PathBuf::from(format!(\"{}{}\", db_path.to_string_lossy(), sidecar));\n1089\t        if p.exists() {\n1090\t            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&p);\n1091\t        }\n1092\t    }\n1093\t\n1094\t    let storage = Storage::open(db_path)?;\n1095\t    let result = storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n1096\t        import_jsonl(jsonl_path, |issue| {\n1097\t            Storage::create_issue_tx(tx, &issue)?;\n1098\t            Ok(UpsertResult::New)\n1099\t        })\n1100\t    })?;\n1101\t    storage.rebuild_blocked_cache()?;\n1102\t    storage.clear_dirty()?;\n1103\t    Ok(result.imported)\n1104\t}\n1105\t\n1106\t/// Layer 6 (restore half) — re-insert snapshotted dirty beads after a rebuild and\n1107\t/// re-mark them dirty. Beads already reconstituted from JSONL are replaced with the\n1108\t/// (newer, unflushed) snapshot version so their in-flight edits survive.\n1109\t///\n1110\t/// Returns the number of beads restored.\n1111\tfn restore_dirty_snapshot(db_path: &Path, snapshot: &[Issue]) -> Result<usize> {\n1112\t    if snapshot.is_empty() {\n1113\t        return Ok(0);\n1114\t    }\n1115\t    let storage = Storage::open(db_path)?;\n1116\t    let now = chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n1117\t    storage.with_immediate_transaction(|tx| {\n1118\t        for issue in snapshot {\n1119\t            if Storage::get_issue_tx(tx, &issue.id)?.is_some() {\n1120\t                // JSONL carried an older copy — overwrite with the unflushed snapshot.\n1121\t                Storage::update_issue_from_json_tx(tx, issue)?;\n1122\t            } else {\n1123\t                Storage::create_issue_tx(tx, issue)?;\n1124\t            }\n1125\t            // Re-mark dirty: these beads are still unflushed relative to JSONL.\n1126\t            tx.execute(\n1127\t                \"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO dirty_issues (issue_id, marked_at) VALUES (?1, ?2)\",\n1128\t                rusqlite::params![issue.id, now],\n1129\t            )?;\n1130\t        }\n1131\t        Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(())\n1132\t    })?;\n1133\t    Ok(snapshot.len())\n1134\t}\n1135\t\n1136\t/// Layered, safe `bf doctor --repair` (Phase 7.2).\n1137\t///\n1138\t/// Walks the six-layer safety stack described above. See [`RepairOptions`] /\n1139\t/// [`RepairReport`].\n1140\tpub fn repair_stack(workspace_dir: &Path, opts: &RepairOptions) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n1141\t    let (beads_dir, db_path, jsonl_path) = resolve_paths(workspace_dir)?;\n1142\t    let mut report = RepairReport::default();\n1143\t\n1144\t    if !jsonl_path.exists() {\n1145\t        return Err(anyhow!(\n1146\t            \"Cannot repair: JSONL file not found at {}\",\n1147\t            jsonl_path.display()\n1148\t        ));\n1149\t    }\n1150\t\n1151\t    // ---- Layer 5: repeat-failure gate (checked before doing any work) ----\n1152\t    if recovery::repair_failed_marker_exists(&beads_dir) && !opts.allow_repeated_repair {\n1153\t        return Err(anyhow!(\n1154\t            \"Refusing to repair: a previous rebuild failed post-verification and its backup was \\\n1155\t             restored (see {}/{}).
